## What changed

Main is red on `plunge_depth_tab::the_tabbed_contour_catalog_case_names_its_tab_window_dives`. Two PRs crossed:

- PR #3866 (#3678) made each tab window dive of the `2d/contour-tabs` catalog case peck one stepdown at a time.

- The verifier names no `PlungeTooDeep` finding for the case.
- The path pecks: tab windows 1 to 3 each dive Z4, Z2, Z0 from the Z6 stock top. No feed goes more than the 2 mm stepdown below the depth before it.

title: feat(ui): browse the holder library in the tool library window
body:
U6 of the tool library redesign (#3663). The tool library window gets a Holders page: the built-in holders by spindle taper and a read-only holder view. This PR also closes the five gaps between U1 to U5 and the mock-up of #3663 (the scope comments on #3897).

Stacked on #3935 (U5). The commits of this PR only: https://github.com/qsmits/Camcraft/compare/b82b017bb...issue/3897-tool-holders-list

Update: #3931 and #3935 merged into `main` (#3935 at its head `b82b017bb`, the base of this branch). The PR diff against `main` now shows the U6 commits only. The gate below merged origin/main `b13ebd440`, before those merges. GitHub reports the PR as mergeable with the current `main` (`02d05bc1c`).

## Two commits, two subjects
The UI refit rule asks for one page or component in each PR. The user decided to fold the mock-up gaps into U6, because each PR is costly on this project. So the PR keeps the rule by commit:
1. `dd129ab43` `feat(ui): close the tool library window's gaps to the mock-up`: the five layout items, their tests and the updated `layout_window_tool_*` tests. It does not build alone, by a split error (see the gate).
2. `3c622f8e5` `feat(ui): browse the holder library in the tool library window`: the Holders page, the used-by query in app, their tests and `layout_window_holders`.

The two belong together because they change the same window: the page switch heads the window, and the wider window and the two-column editor are the frame that the Holders page and the holder view use.

## What changed
Mock-up gaps (commit 1), all display only, no command:
1. **Editor layout.** The tabs and their rows stand on the left, the preview on the right (mock-up picture 2). U3 put the preview above the tabs.
2. **Preview toggles.** "Dimensions" and "Holder" check boxes beside the 3D / Side toggle (view state in `EditorFace`, both on). Holder off: the 3D view shows the model without the holder (`ToolModel::bare`, built with the model), and the side view shows no holder bands and no holder dimension. Dimensions off: the side view draws no dimension line. The flutes toggle comes with #3908.
3. **List rows.** Each Document row starts with a small drawing of the tool (`tool_library_dialog/thumbs.rs`: cached by the tool name and keyed on the tool value; a still frame only moves the kept shapes). A new "Gauge length" column shows the holder's gauge length plus the stick-out for a tool in a library holder. A tool with a drawn body, a mesh body or the stand-in cylinder shows "-", because its gauge line is not stated.
4. **Categories.** U2 did not add them. A column on the left of the list (`categories.rs`) groups the tools by kind under Milling, Hole making, Turning and Other, each category with its count (mock-up picture 1). A category with no tool in the shown source is not listed. A pick filters the rows, as the Tool type choice does (which stays).
5. **Window width.** The window opens `WIDE_W` wide (rail 170 + rows 780 + preview 320 + margins = 1330 px), so the Recipes table and the preview show side by side without a horizontal scroll bar. The window stands left of the Properties pane. On a narrower screen it takes the room left of Properties (it then covers the browser), and the Recipes table scrolls across as before. The minimum width is the same width.

Review fix (commit 3, `29af2e3e1`, the review of `3c622f8e5`):
- On a narrow window the rail folds from 170 px to 120 px (`rail_w`). The preview keeps 250 px while the rows keep 280 px (`columns`).
- The side view's dimension room gives way before the drawing (`side_view::margins`). With Dimensions off, the room is a thin 8 px border. With Dimensions on, the room shrinks in proportion, so the drawing keeps 96 px (`MIN_DRAW`). The painter clips a dimension value at the edge of the area.
- On a 960 px screen the drawing now paints. Before the fix, the side view took its early return and drew nothing.

Holders page (commit 2):
- A "Cutting tools | Holders" switch heads the window. The mock-up says "Tools". "Tools" is already the ribbon cell that opens the window (two buttons of one name break each test and MCP flow that clicks it), and "Tool list" is a browser row. See the decision file.
- `tool_library_dialog/holders.rs`: `holder_library::library()` grouped by taper, the mounted machine's taper (`tooling.spindle_mount`) first and marked "(machine)". Columns: Name, Taper, Clamp, Clamps Ø, Gauge length, Largest Ø, Used by. A taper column on the left ("All holders" and each taper with its count), a name filter, and a note on the mounted machine's taper.
- `tool_library_dialog/holder_view.rs`: the read-only holder view (mock-up picture 5). Machine side (spindle taper, marked when it is the machine's), tool side (clamp and clamping range), shape (gauge length, largest diameter, nose diameter), "Used by N tools" with each tool's stick-out and gauge length (a click opens the tool in the editor), and the outline to scale with its dimension lines and a Dimensions toggle. The outline's shapes and labels are cached on the holder, the rect, the unit and the toggle.
- The view says: "Built-in holders are read-only. User holders and holder edits come with the user library (#3645)." "New holder", Import, Export, edit boxes, Duplicate and Apply on a holder are U7 (#3898).
- App: `tool_body::holder_users(world)` and `tool_body::tools_using_holder(world, entry)`, keyed on `HolderRef::entry` (case and spacing ignored, as `holder_library::find`). A read of the world, so it is in app.
- Decision: `docs/decisions/3897-tool-holders-list.md`.

Commands: none. Browsing, the toggles and the picks are view state. No MCP tool is owed: `get_job` already shows each tool's `holder.library`.

## Readings
Seeded document, the end mill `EM-0600-4FL` put in `BT40 ER32` with the defaults: the list shows "1 tool" on the BT40 ER32 row, and the holder view lists the tool with its stick-out and gauge length. The built-in library groups as BT30, BT40, CAT40, TTS and straight shank. On a 1920 x 1080 screen the window is 1330 px wide; the Recipes table's `fz` column stands left of the preview.

## Pinning tests
New (ui lib, `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/`):
- `tool_library_holders_ui::a_holder_lists_the_tools_that_use_it`: the count in the list, the holder view, the tool link opens the editor, no command.
- `tool_library_holders_ui::the_machine_taper_comes_first_and_a_taper_filters_the_list`
- `tool_library_holders_ui::a_still_frame_builds_no_holder_outline`: counter test, and a changed input builds once.
- `tool_library_mockup::the_preview_toggles_hide_the_dimension_lines_and_the_holder`
- `tool_library_mockup::a_document_row_has_a_cached_drawing_and_its_gauge_length`: gauge value, counter test, a changed tool builds its drawing once.
- `tool_library_mockup::the_categories_filter_the_list`
- `tool_library_mockup::the_window_shows_the_recipes_table_and_the_preview_side_by_side` (1920 x 1080 shell)
- `page_layout_tool_library::layout_window_holders`
- Review fix: `tool_library_mockup::the_side_view_draws_the_tool_on_a_960_px_screen` (960 x 720 shell, Side view, Dimensions on; it also checks `rail_w` and `columns`).
- Review fix: `tool_library_mockup::the_side_view_without_dimensions_takes_their_room_on_a_960_px_screen`.
- The two review-fix tests read a draw counter in `side_view` (`drawn()`), so they fail on the early return. They ran red on `3c622f8e5` ("the Side view painted no drawing (0 -> 0)") and green on `29af2e3e1`.

New (app): `tool_library_holders::used_by::the_used_by_count_counts_tools_by_entry` (in `crates/app/tests/tool_library_holders/used_by.rs`, a `#[path]` module of the existing suite; its gate map now names `app::tool_body`).

Updated: `page_layout_tool_library::layout_window_tool_library` (the switch, the categories left of the rows) and `layout_window_tool_editor` (the preview and its toggles right of the rows).

The `#[test]` count of `crates/ui` goes from 1801 to 1811 (1809 before the review fix). No test is deleted. No snapshot PNG changed.

The tests were written with the code. They were not run red as a separate step, because a red run costs one more full build on the shared Windows machine. During the work, the existing window tests did catch one defect of the new layout: a full-height column separator pushed Apply out of the window. The separator now has the column's height.

## Gate (Windows, winbuild, head 3c622f8e5 merged with origin/main)
- Dry run first: `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main --dry-run` planned 36 steps (app build, app lib, 16 app suites that the `tool_body.rs` gate maps reach, ui build, ui lib, 16 ui suites).
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` (origin/main `b13ebd440`): 36 steps, 36 ok, 0 failed, 0 stalled, wall 10.1 min. ui lib 1629 passed, 0 failed, 8 ignored. app lib 307 passed. `tool_library_holders` 9 passed. The ui lib and `tool_library_holders` steps ran each pinning test above.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: exit 0.
- No heavy step: this issue is P4, not P1. No post or toolpath changed, so no `example_catalog*` suite applies. The light lane was not run.
- **Commit 1 alone does not compile.** When I split the work into two commits, the first commit's `state_tool_library_dialog.rs` lost the `ToolEditorView` struct (`cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui` on `dd129ab43`: E0425/E0422, the type is not found). The branch was already pushed, and this project does not rebase or force-push, so the commit stays as it is. The second commit has the struct, and the final tree is the tree that the gate above tested. A bisect that stops on `dd129ab43` must step to `3c622f8e5`.

## Gate of the review fix (macOS, head `29af2e3e1`)

- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: exit 0. The fix does not touch `camcraft-app`.
- The branch merges cleanly with origin/main (`git merge-tree`), so I did not merge main.

## Not exercised

- An inch document: the holder and gauge values use `units::len`, not pinned in inches.

title: fix(wire): cut DXF arcs and circles as true arcs
body:
## What changed

A Wire Contour on a selected DXF chain with an arc or a circle now cuts. The wire path holds true arcs. The generic ISO, Sodick and G-EDM wire posts write them as G2 / G3 with incremental I J. An exact straight polygon keeps the polygon path of #3180, byte for byte.

### Motion (`crates/motion/src/wire_edm/`)

- New `arc_span.rs`, `arc_chain.rs`: the closed line / arc / circle chain in world XY, walked counter-clockwise. The joint gap tolerance is `JOINT_TOL` = 0.25 µm. A wider gap is refused by name.
- New `arc_offset.rs`: the analytic offset. Each line moves along its normal. Each arc becomes a concentric arc. A pivot arc of the kerf radius about the drawing corner closes each outside corner. A trim at the meet of the two parallels closes each inside corner.
- Refusals by name, never a clamp:
  - an arc on the waste side that is tighter than the kerf offset;
  - a parallel that the trims consume (a slot under the kerf width);
  - a walk that crosses itself (a neck);
  - parallels that do not meet at an inside corner.
- New `arc_cut.rs` (`wire_contour_arcs`): a straight lead to the nearest path point. On a circle the lead is radial. A full circle (or an arc of more than half a turn) is cut as two halves. Each arc goes onto its CL lattice centre (1e-6 mm) with its radius kept. If the centre move, the joint gap and the near-tangent miss together pass 1 nm, the path moves that far to the waste side, and a path note says so.
- New `arc_laws.rs`: the kerf law and the cover law read the drawing itself. The kerf law uses the exact least distance from each recorded move (line, or arc about its lattice centre) to each line and arc of the chain. `laws.rs` only moves the cover refusal text into `uncovered()` (no behaviour change).

### Sim verifier (`crates/sim/src/verify/wire/`)

- New `arcs.rs`: an XY arc move of a vertical cut is read as chords of at most 25 nm sagitta (`ARC_SAG`). Each chord reading is reduced by the chord's sagitta, so an arc whose kerf enters the product never passes.
- An arc on a leaning wire (taper) stays unreadable by name. A tabbed cut with arcs is unreadable by name.

### App (`crates/app/src/operation/`)

- `wire_sketch.rs`: the arc refusal and the exact-gap refusal are removed. `check_path` accepts XY arcs and bounds them by their axis extremes.
- New `wire_sketch_arcs.rs`: routes each chain that is not an exact polygon to `wire_contour_arcs`. The verifier gets the product as a waste-side ring of the chain within 25 nm. `single_pass` still refuses taper, tabs, skims, burnout and 4-axis on a selected chain.
- `generate.rs`, `wire_verify.rs`: the calls to the new routes.

### Post

- No post script changed. `crates/post/src/agie_setup/inspection.rs:1`: the provenance line now says "our own implementation".

## The user's decisions (24 Nov 2026)

1. True arcs, no chord-only step.
2. A start hole exactly at the centre of a die circle: the lead enters towards +X. Rule: of equally near path points, the point at the least counter-clockwise angle from +X wins. A path note says so.
3. **Behaviour change for the maintainer:** TEXT, MTEXT and DIMENSION entities no longer block a selected-chain wire cut. They are not cut, and the wire is not checked against them. A path note gives the count. A HATCH (or any other skipped entity) still refuses, now by its name and count. The native Agie selected-chain door shares this check, so it also accepts a drawing with annotation.
4. Tapered (conical) arcs stay refused. Follow-up: #3941.

A punch on a circle, a racetrack or a tangent loop also takes the arc path now for the generic posts (before: a chord preview). The native Agie job (#2978, #2993) still reads its own `WireProfile`, and its goldens do not change.

## Readings

I read the ISO golden `wire_dxf_die_circle.nc` against the drawing (radius 5 circle, wire 0.25, gap 0.04, k = 0.165; drawing centre posts at X6 Y5):

- the lead goes from X6 Y5 to X10.835 Y5: +X, length 4.835 = 5 - 0.165;
- `G3 X1.165 Y5. I-4.835 J0.`: centre X6 Y5, end at the antipode, counter-clockwise half turn;
- `G3 X10.835 Y5. I4.835 J0.`: centre X6 Y5, back to the seam;
- `G1 X6. Y5.`: the lead-out.

I read `wire_dxf_punch_fillet.nc` (the L punch, drawing turned 90 degrees): the fillet posts as `G3 X13. Y15.165 I-3.165 J0.`, centre X13 Y12 (the drawn centre), radius 3 + 0.165. Each of the four sharp outside corners has a G3 pivot of radius 0.165 about the corner. The inside corner is trimmed to X5.835 Y5.165 (k, k from the corner). The walk is counter-clockwise. The Sodick program starts the cut with a `G01` lead before its first `G03`.

## Pinning tests

- motion `wire_edm::arc_tests` (11): die circle with a centred hole (+X, two half arcs), punch circle (radial seam), line and arc punch (pivots, trim, fillet), line and arc die, inside arc under the offset refused, slot and neck refused, joint gap refused / charged to the margin, off-lattice centre snapped, mutation test (an arc 2 µm into the product fails the kerf law, chords in place of arcs fail the cover law), hole too near or on the wrong side, waste-side ring.
- sim `verify::wire::arc_tests` (3): a die circle of two half arcs passes and frees its slug; an arc 2 µm into the product is a gouge on that arc move; an arc on a leaning wire is unreadable.
- app `wire_dxf_selection` (new module `arcs`, 3 tests, plus the changed pin `curved_pick_survives_and_is_judged_on_its_arcs_and_undo_restores_the_pick`): die circle and line and arc punch through generation, the wire laws, and the ISO, Sodick and G-EDM posts to their goldens; taper on a DXF arc refused; HATCH still refused.

## Gate

Head `ee7270eed`, on the Mac:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: 1,193 steps, 1,192 ok. One step failed: `app suites: rotary_verify` (`a_rough_over_an_oversized_bar_peels_from_the_stock_radius`) at a 1-minute load near 50. This suite does not touch wire code. The test alone passed (58 s), and the step passed again (`--only "app suites: rotary_verify"`, 19 s).
- The plan holds `motion lib`, `sim lib`, `wire_dxf_selection`, `agie_native`, `g_edm_post`, the Sodick and wire suites, and `example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive`, `example_catalog_edge_work` by name: all ok.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-geometry -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo xtask gate light --base origin/main`: 6 steps, all ok (motion light lib, adaptive_troch_island, adaptive_troch_neck, adaptive_troch_parallel, app light pocket_pass_start).

Heavy step (P1 under the safety floor): `cargo xtask gate heavy --base origin/main --dry-run` reaches `app heavy: wire_dxf_selection`, `wire_post` and `wire_stamp`. None of these binaries, and no module of `motion::wire_edm` or `sim::verify::wire`, has an `#[ignore]` heavy test. No heavy test covers this code, so no targeted heavy step exists.

## Not exercised

- No control ran these programs. The goldens are read against the drawing only.
- Tabs, skims, burnout, taper and 4-axis on a DXF chain stay refused (as before). #3617 works on skims and the closing overlap in the same files.
- A short span that an inside trim consumes (for example a short chamfer in a tight inside corner) is refused, not removed.
- Model-based wire cuts still post chords (#3215).

## Goldens moved

All new, none changed:

- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/wire-iso/wire_dxf_die_circle.nc`, `.../wire-iso/wire_dxf_punch_fillet.nc`
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/sodick-wire/wire_dxf_die_circle.nc`, `.../sodick-wire/wire_dxf_punch_fillet.nc`
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/g-edm/wire_dxf_die_circle.nc`, `.../g-edm/wire_dxf_punch_fillet.nc`

Reason: the first arc output of the selected-chain wire path, for each post that writes arcs.

Decision file: `docs/decisions/3937-wire-dxf-arcs.md`.

Changelog: Wire Contour on a selected DXF chain cuts arcs and circles as true G2/G3 arcs (die and punch), with a stated +X entry from the centre of a circle; TEXT, MTEXT and DIMENSION entities no longer block the cut.

Effort: max

title: feat(ui): a Recipes tab for a tool's cutting data per material
body:
U5 of the tool library redesign (#3663). The tool editor of the tool library window gets a Recipes tab. The tab shows the speeds and feeds of a tool for each workpiece material.

Stacked on #3931 (U4). The commits of this PR only: https://github.com/qsmits/Camcraft/compare/9af86ad9f...issue/3896-tool-recipes-tab

The branch has the fixed U4 head `9af86ad9f` merged in (merge `b82b017bb`, no hand edits). That merge closes finding 1 of the review on `9a7f598b5` (the Apply holder refusal now judges the stored tool).

## What changed
- New tab "Recipes" between "Tool" and "Details" (`ToolEditorTab::Recipes`).
- New `tool_library_dialog/recipes_tab.rs` (the tab) and `recipes_fill.rs` (the arithmetic). The tab calls the same cutting rows as Properties (`tool_cutting_rows::cutting_rows_with`). It does not copy them.
- Read-only columns after each speed-and-feed row:
  - surface speed `Vc = pi x D x n / 1000` (m/min, or sfm in an inch document);
  - feed per tooth `fz = F / (n x z)` (mm, or inch);

title: feat(tools)!: a tapered mill has a tip form (sharp, flat, ball)
body:
Plan step D1 of the tool library redesign (#3663). A tapered mill (`ToolKind::Taper`) states its tip form: sharp, flat or ball. The tip math is the research of #895.

## What changed

- **Tool fields.** `Tool` gets `tip_form` (`TaperTip`: `Sharp`, `Flat`, `Ball`; default `Sharp`) and `tip_diameter` (default 0). `corner_r` is the corner radius of a flat tip and the ball radius of a ball tip.
- **Tip math in a new module, `crates/tools/src/taper.rs`.** It holds the tip geometry (`r_flat`, `r_t`, `z_t`, `r0` of #895), the sanity rules by name, the drawn profile and the meridian. `Tool::profile`, `Tool::meridian` and `Tool::why_not_sane` call it. `tools.rs` grows by the field lines and one call. `Tool::geom` does not change: its numbers do not depend on the tip.
- **A sharp taper does not change.** Its profile, meridian and stamp stay bit for bit. Its corner radius stays inert, so an older project with such a tool still opens.
- **Only a chamfer mill states a tip.** Another kind with a non-sharp form or a tip diameter is refused by name. The editor clears the tip fields when the kind changes.
- **Every operation refuses a flat or ball tip by name**, until a generator reads it:
  - at creation, edit and re-tool (`tool_gate::tool_refusal`);
  - at generation and at the post (`tool_gate::tool_problem`). This second door catches a `ChangeTool` that gives the tool of an existing operation a flat tip.
  - The fitting-tool list and the catalog hint do not offer a flat or ball tip. The tool stamp digests the tip form and the tip diameter only for a non-sharp tip.
  - The text: `'CM-0600-90' has a flat tip: the tip form is not read by a Deburr operation yet - use a chamfer mill with a sharp tip`.
- **Files and MCP.** `ToolDto` and the catalog `Def` carry the two fields with `serde(default, skip_serializing_if)`. `add_tool` and `edit_tool` take them through `ToolDto`. `set_tool_cutter_params` takes `tip_form` and `tip_diameter`. `edit_tool` does not call `"tip_form": "sharp"` a lost key. The MCP reference (`docs/agents/mcp-tools.md`) has the new description.
- **Catalog.** Three new tools, common sizes from the public tapered end mill tables: `CM-0600-90-F10` (a flat-tip chamfer mill), `TE-0250-03-F10` (a tapered flat end mill) and `TB-0160-01-R05` (a tapered ball nose).
- **UI.** The Tool tab and Properties show a "Tip form" row for a chamfer mill, and a "Tip diameter" row for a flat tip (new `tool_taper_tip_row.rs`). The edit lands through `ChangeTool` / `AddTool`: one undo step.

## The two version steps (isolated, can be removed)

The user decided on 24 Nov 2026 to step the project-file version too. An older CamCraft reads a flat or ball tip as sharp. A sharp tip is a smaller tool than the real tool, and a toolpath planned for it can gouge. The issue text says "no version step", and the maintainer has not answered the comment on #3368 yet. The user said: "Just start, we can refactor that version step in or out later."

- **`.camproj`**: only a file with a flat or ball tip says `TIP_FORM_PROJECT_VERSION` (79). A file without one still says `PROJECT_VERSION` (78), so an older build opens it as before. This build reads 79 as 78 plus the tip keys.
  - The step is isolated in `crates/app/src/project/file.rs`: `TIP_FORM_PROJECT_VERSION`, `NEWEST_PROJECT_VERSION`, `written_project_version` and `tip_form_read_version`. There is one call in `wire.rs` (save) and one call in `apply.rs` (load).
  - A const assertion stops a later unconditional step from taking 79 by accident.
  - The nine tests that ask for a refused future version now use `NEWEST_PROJECT_VERSION + 1`.
  - To remove the step: delete the four items, write `PROJECT_VERSION` in `wire.rs`, remove the `apply.rs` line, and set the future-version tests back to `PROJECT_VERSION + 1`.
- **`.camtools`**: a library with a flat or ball tip says `TIP_FORM_VERSION` (6). Other libraries keep their older number. Version 5 is kept for the drawn cutter of PR #3906 (`CUTTER_VERSION`). The reader accepts 1 to 4 and 6. The PR that merges second adds the other number to the accepted list.

The decisions are in `docs/decisions/3368-taper-tip-form.md`.

## Breaking change

This PR changes the project file format in a way that older builds cannot read. The fix commit `ee24e1c73` has the `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer.

- A project that holds a flat or ball taper tip is written as `.camproj` version 79. Older CamCraft builds refuse that file.
- A project with only sharp tips stays version 78. Older builds open it as before.
- A tool library with a flat or ball tip is written as `.camtools` version 6.
- The version guard stays. An older build must refuse the tip, because it reads a flat or ball tip as sharp, and a toolpath for that smaller tool can gouge.

## Review fix (finding 1 of the first review)

- A flat or ball taper with a short flute (the flute ends on the cone, under the full diameter) now ends its meridian with the radial shoulder at the flute top. `Tool::profile` draws the same shoulder, so the two agree. Commit `ee24e1c73`, `crates/tools/src/taper.rs` (`meridian_points`).
- Before the fix: a 6 mm taper, 90 degrees, 1 mm flat tip, 1 mm flute had a meridian that ended at r = 1.5 mm. The profile ended at r = 3 mm. A ball tip R0.5 with the same numbers ended at r = 1.2071 mm.
- The drawn profile (`taper::outline`) already had the shoulder. No other code builds the tip geometry.
- A sharp taper does not change. `meridian::tests::a_sharp_taper_keeps_its_profile_and_digest` passes.

## Readings

- Flat tip, 10 mm, 60 degrees, tip 4 mm, corner 0.5 mm: `r_flat` = 1.711 mm, the tangent point is on the cone line `r = r0 + z tan(30)`, and the cone meets the 5 mm radius at z = 5.196 mm.
- Ball tip, R0.5, 1 degree a side: the tangent point is on the ball and on the cone (both to 1e-9).

## Pinning tests

- `camcraft-tools` lib: `taper::tests::short_flat_profile_and_meridian_agree` and `taper::tests::short_ball_profile_and_meridian_agree` (review fix; red before the fix with the reviewer's numbers, green after). `meridian::tests::a_flat_and_a_ball_taper_meridian_agrees_with_the_profile` has the two short-flute tools too (it also builds their solid atoms).
- `camcraft-tools` lib: `taper::tests::*` (11 tests: the tip math, the named refusals, the profile, the meridian, the catalog tools, the words).
- `camcraft-tools` lib: `meridian::tests::a_sharp_taper_keeps_its_profile_and_digest` (every shipped sharp taper and one with an inert corner radius, against the profile code before this PR), `meridian::tests::a_flat_and_a_ball_taper_meridian_agrees_with_the_profile`.
- `crates/app/tests/tool_law.rs`: `every_operation_refuses_a_non_sharp_taper_by_name`.
- `crates/app/tests/mcp_deburr.rs`: `a_deburr_refuses_its_tool_after_a_flat_tip_edit` (the generation door).
- `crates/app/tests/tool_library.rs`: `a_tip_form_round_trips_and_steps_the_version`.
- `crates/app/tests/project_roundtrip.rs`: `a_tip_form_round_trips_and_steps_the_project_version`.
- `crates/app/tests/mcp_edit_tool.rs`: `edit_tool_sets_the_tip_form` (also `set_tool_cutter_params`).
- `camcraft-ui` lib: `tool_library_editor::the_tip_form_row_shows_for_a_taper`, `tool_taper_tip_row::tests::*`.

## Gate (macOS, final head ee24e1c73)

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: **117 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled** (18.0 min). This includes `tools suites: lib`, `app suites: example_catalog*`, `app suites: golden_cl` and `ui suites: lib`.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-tools -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `git merge-tree --write-tree HEAD origin/main`: no conflict.
- Env: `CAMCRAFT_NO_SEED=1`, `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=6`. No heavy step (P4).

## Earlier gate (Windows, winbuild, head 597460ab3)

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: **117 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled** (24.4 min). The plan expected 40 to 60. The Tool struct literals in test helpers of `motion::drilling` and the `catalog.json` change pull the drilling suites and `example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive` and `example_catalog_edge_work` (all green). It does not go to the full batch.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-tools -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo xtask gate light`: 6 steps, 0 failed (on 40c28a009; the later commits change only app test files).
- The first gate run had 2 red steps (a missed future-version test in `pocket_no_adaptive.rs`, and a combo query in the new UI test). Both are fixed; the second run is green.
- Env: `CAMCRAFT_NO_SEED=1`, `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=5`. No heavy step (P4).
- The tests were written first (commit edaba30e5). They were red by compile (the fields did not exist); they were not run red.

## Not exercised

- No generator, stock simulation or collision law reads a flat or ball tip yet. Each operation refuses such a tool by name. The consumer sub-issues of #3351 open those doors (#3370, #3371, #3373).
- The `camcraft-mcp` skill row for `set_tool_cutter_params` (a process file) does not list the two new params. The tool description and `docs/agents/mcp-tools.md` do.
- The setup sheet and the tool table exports do not show the tip form.

## Screenshots (rendered headlessly with egui_kittest on Windows)

## What changed

- `crates/app/tests/plunge_depth_tab.rs` pins two cases. No production code changes.
- `the_tabbed_contour_catalog_case_pecks_its_tab_window_dives` (renamed from `the_tabbed_contour_catalog_case_names_its_tab_window_dives`):

  - No step bites more than the 2 mm stepdown below the Z 6 stock top or below the depth before it.
- `a_tabbed_contour_under_carried_stock_names_its_deep_dives` (new):
  - The same case, with the contour top 4 mm under the stock top. The test sets it with `EditOperationParams`.
  - The verifier names four dives. Each is a feed plunge that lands on Z 2 and bites 4 mm against the 2 mm stepdown.
  - No finding holds the post.
  - This keeps the #3679 law pinned end to end through the app (stepdown wiring, generate, cached warnings).
- `docs/decisions/3925-plunge-tab-pin.md` records the choice.

## Cause

PR #3847 (#3679) and PR #3866 (#3678) merged one minute apart. #3866 pecks the three tab window dives. The verifier then correctly names no dive. The test expectation from #3847 was out of date. The toolpath is correct.

## Tests

title: fix(ai): show key rejected after a provider authentication failure
body:
## What changed

The provider Test control now shows a distinct "key rejected" status when a
cloud provider rejects the key, instead of one shared failure text.

- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/ai_chat/settings_text.rs`: a new `is_auth_failure`
  rule classifies the authentication failure before the generic status match.
  The rule is:
  - HTTP 401 or 403: authentication failure, for every cloud provider behind
    Test (Anthropic, OpenAI Chat, OpenAI Responses, Gemini).
  - Any other status: key rejected only when the provider error carries one of
    its documented classified auth fields: `authentication_error` (Anthropic
    `error.type`), `invalid_api_key` (OpenAI `error.code`), `api_key_invalid`
    or `UNAUTHENTICATED` (Gemini `error.status`), or Gemini's documented plain
    message "API key not valid". Gemini answers a bad key with HTTP 400, not
    401; without this shape Gemini would show the generic request failure.
  - The status line reads `Test failed: the key was rejected (HTTP <code>).`
    The provider response text is never shown beyond the already redacted
    classified fields, and the key is removed before any of this runs
    (`http.rs` redacts before truncation, unchanged).
- Other failures keep their own statuses, distinct from key rejected: wrong
  model (404 or 400/422 without an auth marker), billing or credits (402 or a
  billing marker), rate limit (429), provider outage (5xx), network, and an
  invalid Model name.
- `crates/app/tests/ai_http_review.rs`: pin that each provider's transport
  surfaces the HTTP authentication status and never the key.

## Classification note (conservative cases)

HTTP 403 can also mean a permission or region denial, not a bad key. The rule
still reports key rejected for 403: the hint ("paste a new key") names the
most common cause, and no provider here returns 403 for a credit or model
failure. A 400 is only key rejected through the documented marker, never
guessed, so a wrong model on Gemini stays a model failure.

## Pinning tests

- `egui_app::tests::ai_chat::settings_failure_details::authentication_failure_shows_key_rejected_for_each_cloud_provider`
- `egui_app::tests::ai_chat::settings_failure_details::gemini_bad_request_with_documented_key_error_shows_key_rejected`
- `egui_app::tests::ai_chat::settings_failure_details::non_auth_cloud_test_failures_remain_distinct_from_key_rejected`
- `egui_app::tests::ai_chat::settings_hand_test::failed_test_names_the_cause_the_model_and_what_to_try` (updated wording)
- `authentication_failure_surfaces_the_http_status_for_each_cloud_provider` (`camcraft-app`, `ai_http_review`)

## Gate

- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test ai_http_review`: 7 passed.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --lib`: 307 passed.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib`: 1612 passed, 8 ignored.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised

The live-ai lane (#3803) does not exist yet. Its wrong-key step ("Use a wrong
key and confirm the key rejected status") is already specified there and was
not run here; every pin above runs over loopback HTTP fixtures, not real
credentials or remote services. The Gemini 400 marker path is pinned from the
published API error shape, not from a live provider answer.

Changelog: AI Chat: the provider Test shows a key rejected status after an authentication failure, with other causes kept distinct.

title: feat(ui): add, move and remove the axes of a machine in the file editor
body:
The Machines pane's file editor gets an "Axis chain" group. The group adds, moves and removes the axis parts of a `.mch` file, reverses a linear axis, and sets the direction of a rotary axis. The editor changes the file's own JSON, so it keeps every key that it does not know. The decisions and the open questions are in `docs/decisions/2756-machine-axis-chain.md`.

![The Axis chain group on a 3-axis mill, above General](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/roer70/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/2756/axis-chain.png)

## What changed

- **`MachineDraft`** (`crates/app/src/machine/chain.rs`, `draft.rs`) adds, moves and removes axis parts in `kinematics.default.parts`, like `add_coolant` and `remove_coolant`. A refused edit changes nothing. The validator judges the result as before.
  - A new axis goes **on the table** (beside the table's axes, before the head; a rotary there turns the work) or **carries the head** (it takes the head's slot; a rotary there tilts the tool).
  - **Remove** keeps what the axis carried: its `parts` take its place, in order. Its controller row goes with it.
  - **Up and Down** trade an axis with its neighbour row. The tree keeps its shape, so a move never changes which slot carries the head. An axis keeps all its own keys (`pivot`, `offset`, `zero_offset`, `rollover`, `sign_convention`, unknown keys) and gets the `parent` and `chain_order` (#1962) of its new slot.
  - A move trades only with an axis of the same kind (rotary or linear) that moves the same thing (the work or the tool). Other moves are refused, and the refusal says to remove the axis and add it again.
  - A linear is reversed with `"direction": -1` (#373). Back to standard removes the key.
  - A rotary's `axis` is ±X, ±Y, ±Z or three numbers. The editor suggests the RS-274 letter (about X is A, about Y is B, about Z is C) and adds a note to a row whose letter does not agree. It does not refuse it.
- **The validator** keys the work-length refusals by axis and key (`A nose_to_axis`, `work_length_refusals` in `crates/post/src/machine/swing.rs`), so each refusal shows at its row and not above the grid. The rule is the parser's own rule.
- **The editor rows** (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/machine_axis_chain.rs`) draw in one property grid, like General and the editor's other groups (`prop_grid` in `layout/form.rs`, #1122): one setting per row, the label in the first column and the control beside it, help as a hover text. A first version pushed the controls to the right edge (`prop_row`), so in a wide pane they drifted away from their labels. Each axis has a row with its letter and kind and the buttons Up, Down and ✖. Their accessible names are "Move A up", "Move A down" and "Remove A". The direction and the place of a new axis are dropdowns.
  - `nose_to_axis` (#804) and `axis_to_table` (#1107) are rows for a rotary that turns the work. A rotary that carries the head shows them only when the file states one, so that the user can clear it.
  - A row whose `offset` has no parent rotary gets a note (see Q1 below).
  - The fields have stable ids, so a note or a refusal that comes or goes above a field does not take the focus while the user types.
- The Machines pane's editor and detail view fill the width of the pane.

The machine window ("edit a machine" from the Setup pane) also has "add axis". That window edits the mounted `Machine` (a flat list of axes and limits) through `EditMachineApply`. This group edits the axis tree of the `.mch` file and keeps the keys that the editor does not know. They are two different tools, and this PR does not change the machine window.

## Open questions (the decision file takes the recommended option)

The maintainer has not answered these yet. Each one has a cost to change in the decision file.

- **Q1** (comment of 2026-11-20): an `offset` on a rotary with no parent rotary. This PR shows a note at the row and does not refuse the file. We recommend a refusal in the validator.
- **Q2** (comment of 2026-11-20): a move trades only with an axis of the same kind. This PR also refuses a trade between an axis that moves the work and one that moves the tool.
- The three questions in the issue: the order with #1970, the #785 pair beside the #1962 pair, and a machine with a tilting head and a rotary table. This PR adds a head axis and a table axis to the same file, but does not draw a "Kinematics" group.

## Readings

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on `e0e4fee68`: 124 steps, 0 failed, 7.5 min.
- `cargo xtask gate light --base upstream/main` on `e0e4fee68`: 4 steps, 0 failed, 5.0 min.
- The gate's batch plan, run one step at a time, on `303188d61` (before the last merge of main): 1,073 steps. One red step was `a_kind_that_is_not_a_kind_refuses_at_the_door`, which main has since fixed ("router" is now a kind). The suite `machine` is green after the merge.
- No heavy step: the issue is `P6`, not `P1` under the safety floor.

## Pinning tests

31 new tests, none removed. The new app tests are modules of the existing `machine` suite (`crates/app/tests/machine/`), so this PR adds no test binary (#3187).

- `crates/app/tests/machine/axis_chain.rs` (15): add on the table and with the head, remove, move, the refusals, unknown keys kept, and `a_rotary_that_turns_the_work_never_trades_with_one_that_tilts_the_tool`.
- `crates/app/tests/machine/axis_rows.rs` (9): what each row says, the RS-274 letter note, the offset note, reverse, turn about, and the work lengths.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/machines_axis_chain.rs` (7): the group through AccessKit labels: an A added on the table, moved and saved; a refused letter and a remove; X reversed and set back; a turn about Y that suggests B and a note for an A about Y; the FlexiHAL router built from a blank mill and saved; the offset note; and a field that keeps its focus when a refusal goes away.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/machines_edit.rs`: `pick_kind` scrolls the dropdown into view first, because the group makes the form taller.

## Not exercised

- The offset-note UI test was written after the note, so it was not seen red first.
- No output was posted from a machine file that this editor wrote. The values feed the clearance gates and the post kinematics through `parse_mch`, which the app tests check.
- The "Kinematics" group (`pivot`, `offset`, `zero_offset`, `rollover`, `controller.rtcp` as fields) is #1970's. This PR keeps those keys on every edit and does not draw them.
- `validate.rs`, `egui_app/mod.rs`, `egui_app/tests.rs` and `tests/machine.rs` are over 400 lines on main. This PR adds 1, 1, 1 and 9 lines to them.

Changelog: The Machines file editor adds, moves and removes the axes of a machine, reverses a linear axis and sets a rotary's direction.

Fixes #2756

title: fix(contour): enter every wall-side ring by the ramp, not the pass link plunge
body:
Stacked on #3834 (merge #3834 first).

## What changed

- `contour_link::ring_entry` now applies on the wall side too. On the wall side it applies to the Ramp and Helix arms only.
- `contour::emit_band` calls `ring_entry` for each untabbed ring after the first ring of a level, inside or outside.
- An outside ring after another ring now goes through `engage_level`. It takes the wall-side ramp of #3833 (`contour_wall_ramp`).
- The helix stands down to that ramp. It says so in its one existing note.
- The traverse between the parts rides the pass link plane (`Step::traverse` from #3834). Pass `Clearance` crosses at `clearance_z`. Pass `Retract` crosses at the hop plane.
- These stay as before:
  - the wall-side Arc entry (its own hop and wall arc);
  - tabbed levels;
  - the Plunge entry;
  - a `KeepDown` pass link that holds its proof (it feeds straight across);
  - a ring that is too short for the ramp angle (it grazes, with the existing "too short" note).
- Decision: `docs/decisions/3917-contour-outside-ring-entry.md`.

## Cause

`ring_entry` returned `None` on the wall side. Thus each ring after the first ring at a level took `ring_link`. That link lifts, crosses and plunges straight down at the plunge feed. It posts no note.

## Readings

The pin uses the `outside_ramped` fixture: tool 10 mm, stepdown 1 mm, 3 levels, bottom Z -3, ramp 5 degrees, 16 mm square parts 40 mm apart.

| Entry | 2 parts (before / after) | 3 parts (before / after) |
|---|---|---|
| Ramp 5 deg, axial dives | 3 / 0 | 6 / 0 |
| Plunge, axial dives | 6 / 6 | 9 / 9 |

Before the fix, the notes were empty (`[]`).

## Tests

- Pin: `every_outside_ring_of_several_parts_is_entered_by_the_wall_side_ramp` (`camcraft-motion`, `tests/machining2d.rs`).
  - It covers 2 and 3 parts, Ramp and Helix, and pass `Clearance` and pass `Retract`.
  - It asserts: no axial dive, no `Plunge` move, the steepest descent is at most 5 degrees, and each ring-to-ring crossing rides the pass link plane.
- Red before the fix: yes. On the #3834 head the pin fails: `2 parts, Ramp, pass Clearance: no ring dives: []`, left 3, right 0.
- Mutation: I put back `ring_to_ring && inside && !tabbed` at the call site. The pin fails with the same message. I restored the fix. The pin passes.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on the final head: 43 steps, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo xtask gate light --base upstream/main`: 6 steps, 0 failed.
- `camcraft-app` suites `example_catalog` (41 pass, 4 ignored heavy), `example_catalog_adaptive` (1 pass), `example_catalog_edge_work` (1 pass).
- Heavy lanes: not run. This is a `P3` PR. AGENTS.md "Heavy lanes at review" gives a heavy step only to a `P1` PR.

## Goldens moved

None. I ran the example catalog suites above. No `*.nc`, `*.cl` or `examples/catalog/**` file changed.

## Not exercised

- No end-to-end app or post test with several outside parts. The pin is at the motion level.
- No UI change, so no screenshots.

## Overlaps

- Stacked on #3834. It changes the same functions: `contour::emit_band` (the `ring_entry` call) and `contour_link::ring_entry`. Retarget is not needed: this PR already targets `main`. Merge #3834 first.
- #3912 touches `crates/motion/tests/machining2d.rs`, in other tests. Whichever merges second refreshes.

Effort: high

Changelog: 2D Contour outside: each ring after the first ring at a level is now entered by the Ramp or Helix entry, not by an axial plunge with no note.

Fixes #3917

title: feat(tools): add metric tap-drill and clearance drills, a 3 mm ball and a 6 mm bull nose to the catalog
body:
## What changed

The starter tool catalog (`assets/tools/catalog.json`) gets 16 tools:

- `BN-0300`: a 3 mm ball end mill.
- `BB-0600-R1`: a 6 mm bull nose end mill with a 1 mm corner radius.
- 14 jobber drills: a tap drill and a clearance drill (ISO 273 medium) for each coarse thread from M3 to M12.

| Thread | Tap drill | Clearance drill |
|---|---|---|
| M3 | `DR-0250` | `DR-0340` |
| M4 | `DR-0330` | `DR-0450` |
| M5 | `DR-0420` | `DR-0550` |
| M6 | `DR-0500` | `DR-0660` |
| M8 | `DR-0680` | `DR-0900` |
| M10 | `DR-0850` | `DR-1100` |
| M12 | `DR-1020` | `DR-1350` |

Each new tool goes into its family in diameter order. The other tools keep their order.

The cutting data follows the rules of the catalog's own rows. Below 6 mm, the drill rpm and feed are interpolated between `DR-0200`, `DR-0300`, `DR-0400` and `DR-0600`. Thus a larger drill never turns faster than a smaller drill. From 6 mm up, the drills use the cutting speed and the feed per revolution of `DR-0600`. `docs/decisions/3036-metric-catalog.md` gives each rule and its source.

The drill flute length is 3 x D on a 0.5 mm step. A length such as 9.9 mm made `spun::tests::a_parametric_holder_stacks_bit_identically_to_the_cylinder` fail: the spun holder band length was 35.00000000000001 and the cylinder was 35.0. A length on a 0.5 mm step is exact in binary. This PR does not change the spun holder code.

## How tested

- `cargo xtask gate quick`: green (`tools suites: lib`, `app suites: mcp`).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-tools -p camcraft-app --tests -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Pinning tests:
  - `catalog_asset_tests::the_catalog_carries_the_metric_hole_drills_and_small_ball_tools` (sizes, kind, flute length, and the rpm order of all drills).
  - `catalog_asset_tests::the_shipped_asset_parses_and_every_tool_is_valid` (the new `ORDER`).
  - `mcp::add_tool_picks_the_metric_hole_drills_and_small_ball_tools_by_name` (`list_tool_catalog` shows each tool, and `add_tool` adds it by name).

## Not exercised

- No air cut or real cut with the new tools.
- The tool picker in the GUI was not opened. The picker reads the same catalog list.

Changelog: Tool catalog: a 3 mm ball, a 6 mm bull nose, and the metric tap-drill and clearance drills for M3-M12.

title: feat(ui): the tool library window shows the tool as an orbitable 3D model and a to-scale side view
body:
## What changed

This is U3 of #3663, with the scope that the user decided on 24 Nov 2026. The maintainer (Sgt_Hindsight) said: "as long as we keep the 3D preview bit, im aiming to develop on that down the line" / "as running weirdly shape tools requires models" / "not just a spun profile". Thus the old U3 (a large 2D drawing with painted flute helix lines) is replaced. The painted helix lines are dropped. Helical flutes on the 3D model are the follow-up #3908.

- The editor of the tool library window has a preview area above its Tool and Details tabs. It has two views and a toggle ("3D" / "Side"):
  - **3D (the default):** the tool as an orbitable model (drag to turn, scroll to zoom, double-click to fit). A tool with a landed body shows the steel revolved up to the body, and then the body's own facets. A tool without a body shows the steel and the holder cylinder, both revolved. Thus the view is never empty. The steel is the landed drawn cutter (`ToolCutter`, carried onto the draft numbers), else `Tool::profile` up to the shank top. A caption says where the model comes from.
  - **Side (to scale):** the side drawing of `tool_preview` at the size of the editor, with dimension lines: diameter, flute length, shank (Ø × length), stick-out (tip to holder face), gauge (tip to holder top) and holder (Ø × length). No helix lines.
- The renderer of the body placement view (#371) moves into its own module, `egui_app/tool_model_view.rs` (`View`, `project`, `gesture`, `apply`), so that the maintainer can build on it. The placement view uses it. Pick tip and Pick axis stay on the tool page and do not change (`placement_view`). The orbit is one value, `state::Orbit`.
- `preview_inputs` returns a landed drawn cutter on each tab, not only under "Draw cutter" (#93 leftover). This also fixes the Properties preview. After the review, `preview_inputs` is in its own module, `egui_app/tool_preview_inputs.rs` (moved out of `tool_profile_page.rs`).
- Frame cost of the Properties preview (review fix): the cutter check and its outline are a memo keyed on the draft tool value and the cutter draft points, not on `doc_version`. The piece is named `ui/properties.tool.cutter_outline` with `frame_cost::span`. A still Properties frame checks no cutter.
- `tool_preview::draw` is split into `paint` (draws into a given rect, gives the scale) and `draw`. The Properties preview paints the same pixels as before.
- Frame cost (`crates/ui/AGENTS.md`): the model (steel, bands, mesh, mesh box, dimensions) is a memo keyed on the draft tool, the document's tool, the landed cutter and the landed body (facets by `Arc` identity). The projected screen mesh is a second memo keyed on the model mesh, the rect and the orbit. Neither keys on `doc_version`. The piece is named `ui/tool_library.preview` with `frame_cost::span`. A still frame builds and projects nothing.
- The window's preview reads the landed body and cutter by the draft's name. It never syncs the Properties body or cutter drafts, so the window can show a different tool.

title: fix(motion): refuse a Linear comp lead whose dive rides the ring before G41/G42
body:
## What changed

- `contour_comp::door` (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/contour_comp.rs`) refuses a 2D Contour under control or wear compensation when its lead-in or its lead-out is `Linear`. The refusal names the mode and the end, for example: "control compensation does not ride a Linear lead-in - the entry's descent at its start runs on the ring's own offset before G41/G42 engages, so a register over the nominal radius, or a positive wear value, cuts the finished wall there; pick the Perpendicular lead-in, or Computer compensation".
- The rule covers both ends: the mirrored lead-out has the same defect at its end, because the cancel withdrawal lands on the ring line past G40.
- The straight-lead refusal no longer offers the Linear shape, and the approach page's consequence line says the same (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/approach_page.rs`).
- The existing comp fixtures moved from the Linear lead to the Perpendicular lead; the four control-comp and four wear-comp G-code goldens were regenerated. The dive point in each golden moves from `(11, -3)` - one nominal radius off the part, the defect - to `(5, -9)`, the radius plus the lead. The compensated ring itself did not move.
- Decision: `docs/decisions/3891-comp-entry-wall.md`. Refusal over proof: no law bounds the operator's register, and a Linear lead's dive point stands ON the ring's offset line, so no register over the nominal (plus the stock) is safe there. Refusal over an engage reorder: RS-274 / ISO 6983 builds the offset over a straight XY block, so an axial plunge or a vertical-plane arc cannot carry G41/G42. Refusal over a moved dive point: a new lead shape with a new room-law proof.

Builds on the Ramp/Helix refusal of #3890, now in `main`: this branch carries that commit as its base, and its fixtures now use the Perpendicular lead (its pins still pass).

## The geometry reading

- Between the end of the rapid and the first move with G41/G42 active, the Plunge entry posts one axial dive at the lead-in's start, and the Arc entry posts a vertical-plane arc whose XY footprint is the straight chord onto that same point (`entry_arc`).
- A `Linear` lead starts ON the ring's own offset line: one nominal radius plus the stock off the finished wall. The machine runs those moves at the nominal centre under G40, so a register over the nominal radius, or a positive wear value over the stock, cuts the finished wall at the dive point (and at the cancel's end) before G41/G42 engages. The old golden showed it: the dive at `(11, -3)` against the 10 x 10 part, 3 mm off the wall.
- A `Perpendicular` lead starts its length further into the air. The door's length law (at least the tool radius, re-checked on the actual move by `push_span`) holds that at one full radius, so every pre-engage position keeps at least (radius + lead length) off the finished wall. That is the maximum register difference the door vouches for: the register must sit one full radius over the nominal before the wall is at risk.
- The bore side reads the same: under compensation the plunge's `disc_clears` test always takes the lead start (the door guarantees the lead length), so the bore's dive and the bore-side arc chord stand the same clearance inside the bore.
- The Ramp and Helix entries and level transitions were already refused by #3890; their cases are covered, on both sides, and this PR's pins confirm those refusals still fire with the Perpendicular fixture.

## Pinning tests

- `crates/motion/tests/machining2d.rs` `a_linear_lead_under_control_or_wear_is_refused_by_name_on_both_sides`: lead-in and lead-out, Control and Wear, Side::Outside and Side::Inside; the same parameters in Computer generate.
- `crates/motion/tests/machining2d.rs` `the_perpendicular_comp_entry_keeps_the_lead_length_beyond_the_ring`: Control and Wear, both sides, Plunge and Arc entry - every cut-adjacent move before each span's engage stands at least the radius (5) plus the lead (6) off the part, and the closest position is the dive point itself. The bore side is pinned here because a whole-model source posts only the wall side.
- `crates/app/tests/control_comp.rs` `a_linear_lead_in_or_out_under_control_or_wear_is_refused_and_posts_nothing`: through `GenerateOperation`; no toolpath is stored and the post gate writes no G41/G42 program.
- `crates/app/tests/control_comp.rs` `the_entry_descents_before_g41_hold_the_wall_clear_under_an_oversized_register_and_positive_wear`: reads the posted Fanuc program. An oversized register (5.0 mm on the D6 tool, 2 mm over its nominal 3) and a positive wear value (1.0 mm, effective radius 4.0) do not touch the finished wall at any stand under G40; the closest stand is the dive point at 9 mm, the radius plus the lead. Plunge and Arc entries, Control and Wear.

## What was not exercised

- A posted bore-side program: no whole-model fixture in the app tests yields an inside ring, so the bore side is pinned on the CL positions (the exact moves the post writes under G40) at the motion level.
- The stands are checked as positions, not swept segments: the fixture's under-G40 segments are vertical plunges at a fixed XY and one diagonal rapid at clearance height, so the endpoints cover them.
- The register values are modeled in the test (the machine's D register is not part of the program text); the CL carries the nominal radius only, by design.

## Gate

- The mapped suites, run by hand at `-j 8`: `camcraft-motion` lib (619 passed, 22 ignored - heavy lane), `climb_direction` (9), `contour_start_comp` (5), `control_comp` (8), `machining2d` whole suite (75), `wear_comp` (2); `camcraft-app` lib (306) and the touched suites `control_comp` (9), `wear_comp` (5); `camcraft-ui` lib (1588 passed, 8 ignored - snapshot lane) and the eight suites the gate map names for `ui::egui_app::approach_page` (boundary 3, boundary_picks 7, contour_dxf_sketch 2, sinker_setup 2, tap_hand 3, theme_example 3, theme_files 17, waterjet_tool 1). Clippy `-p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- The full `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` could not complete on this machine. Its plan falls back to the whole `camcraft-app` and `camcraft-ui` suite sets (766 steps) because the G-code goldens under `tests/golden/` count as shared test inputs - that fallback builds every app test binary, about 90 GB, and the link failed at 1.1 GB free (`LNK1180`, `LNK1318`). The goldens this PR changes are read by exactly the two app suites above, which ran green twice (with and without `WRITE_GOLDEN=1`).
- sccache's wrapper crashed rustc (`STATUS_STACK_BUFFER_OVERRUN`) at this machine's full parallelism early in the session; every build after that used no wrapper and a lowered job budget.

Changelog: 2D Contour under control or wear compensation refuses a Linear lead-in or lead-out by name - its dive point runs on the ring's own offset, where a register over the nominal radius cuts the finished wall before G41/G42 engages; the Perpendicular lead stays legal and its clearance is pinned from the posted G-code.

Effort: high

Fixes #3891

body:
A new developer page, `site/content/developers/ai-agents.md` ("Contributing with AI agents", Developers section, after Releases). It is for outside contributors. It collects what we learned when we used Claude Code and other agents on this project. It gives no maintainer procedure.

Sections:

- **Your first hour:** say hello on Discord, what to install (GitHub CLI, Rust, the Linux packages, an AI agent and its cost, disk), fork and clone, run the app with a sample part, a link to good first issues, and `/work-issue`.
- **Getting started with Claude Code:** `AGENTS.md` is read automatically, the project skills, and the MCP server.
- **From issue to main:** look at what is open first, claim by comment, branch, pinning test, quick gate, draft PR with the body checklist (`Changelog:`, `Fixes #N`, `Process change: yes`, screenshots on an images-only fork branch, a reason for a new test binary), review, merge. A series starts with its shape.
- **Tips and gotchas:** disk per worktree, sccache and `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`, one gate for each checkout, failures that also fail on bare main, Windows and macOS notes.
- **More than one computer** and **Using subagents.**
- **Not a coder?** The issues are the backlog (read, comment, file good issues, check fixes). Contribute with designs (own models only, no vendor CAD).
- **I have a CNC machine:** the shipped machine files and posts, what to send for a missing machine, and the first cut is an air cut.
- **Clean room:** what we can use and what we cannot read (output, posts, tool libraries, screenshots or help text of other CAM products).
- **Your agent helps with more than code**, **If something is unclear**, **We are all volunteers**, and a **FAQ** (no Rust, AGENTS.md is long, fear of breaking things, cost and time, small computers, machine owners, overwhelmed).
- **Where to talk:** the CamCraft Discord and craftydevs.org.

Three ideas are adapted from SolidCraft's contributor guide (Apache-2.0). The page credits them.

The page gives general learnings only. It has no machine names, accounts or private details. It says that `AGENTS.md` is authoritative.

title: fix(ui): one locked, shared GPU device for the trace test binaries
body:
## What changed

- `crates/ui/src/headless_gpu.rs` now holds the process GPU lock (`gpu_guard`, `gpu_holders`).
- A new `headless_gpu::test_gpu(suite)` takes the lock and returns the one device of the process.
- The device is made one time (`OnceLock`, through `device_for_test` and its SKIP policy). It is never dropped.
- `tests/trace_composite.rs` and `tests/trace_parity.rs` use `test_gpu` in each test. They do not make their own device now.
- The lib test `view_pass::tests::fit_target_never_asks_the_device_for_a_texture_past_its_limit` uses `test_gpu`. Before, it made a device with no lock.
- The three ignored GPU tests take `gpu_guard()` as their first statement:
  - `render_all_guide_images` (`tests/guide_images.rs`)
  - `review_1710_wcs_page_and_viewport_evidence` (`tests/review_1710_evidence.rs`)
  - `generate_evidence_screenshots` (`viewport_bar_tooltip_tests.rs`)
- `egui_app::gpu_test_lock` re-exports the lock from `headless_gpu`. The lib tests and the shared device take the same one lock.
- `docs/decisions/3605-gpu-test-device-lock.md` records the decision.

## Cause

Each test in the two trace binaries made and dropped its own wgpu device. The tests run on parallel test threads with no lock. On a hybrid-GPU Windows laptop (Intel Arc 140T + NVIDIA RTX 5050), two or more devices were alive at the same time. Both binaries ended with `0xC0000005`.

## Tests

Pins (lib, `egui_app::gpu_test_lock`):
- `devices_asked_from_many_threads_are_one_device_used_one_at_a_time`: 8 threads ask for the device 4 times each, at the same time. Each must be the only holder. All must get the same device. Each makes a buffer and submits under the lock.
- `the_trace_binaries_share_one_locked_device`: a source scan. `trace_composite.rs` and `trace_parity.rs` must call `test_gpu` and must not call `device_for_test(`, `headless_gpu::device(` or `request_device(`.
- `every_gpu_test_takes_the_lock`: the table now has 12 tests (4 new). Each must start with `gpu_guard()` or take `test_gpu`.

Red before the fix, and mutation results (each restored after, then green):
- Old call sites (the six test files from `upstream/main`): `the_trace_binaries_share_one_locked_device` FAILED (`tests/trace_composite.rs: takes the shared device through test_gpu`). `every_gpu_test_takes_the_lock` FAILED (`view_pass.rs: ... found "let Some(gpu) = crate::headless_gpu::device_for_test(...)"`).
- Lock removed (`gpu_guard` locks a new mutex each call): `devices_asked_from_many_threads_...` FAILED alone (`a second test holds the GPU`). `the_lock_lets_one_holder_in_at_a_time` and `a_panic_with_the_lock_held_...` FAILED too.

title: fix(app): a tool library file keeps a tool's drawn cutter
body:
## What changed

A tool library file (`.camtools`) now keeps the drawn cutter (`ToolCutter`) of a tool. Before this change, export and import dropped it.

- `crates/app/src/tool_library.rs`:
  - `export_tool_library` writes the drawn cutter as `cutter`. These are the `[z, r, arc]` points that a `.camproj` tool stores.
  - A file with one or more cutters says version 5 (`CUTTER_VERSION`). A file without a cutter keeps version 4 or lower.
  - `parse_tool_library` reads `cutter` and judges it with `cutter_profile::check`. This is the same check as the project loader (`cutter_from_dto`). A cutter that disagrees with its tool, or a malformed cutter, refuses the whole file by tool name.
  - `LibraryTool` has a new field `cutter`.
- `crates/app/src/commands/tool_import/mod.rs`: `ImportTools` sets the cutter on Add, Update and Replace. Undo restores the previous cutter in the same undo step. A library tool without a cutter keeps the cutter of the document on Update (the same law as the body). A tool that is the same in all but its cutter is now an update, not a skip.
- No `.camproj` change: the project file carries `cutter` since #93 slice 2.
- `crates/app/src/tool_table.rs`: the new field (`cutter: None`).
- `crates/app/tests/holder_reference.rs`: the "future version" of an existing test is now `CUTTER_VERSION + 1`.

A build that reads version 1 to 4 refuses a version-5 file: `tool library version 5 is not supported (this build reads 1 to 4)`. It does not drop the cutter silently. title: fix(3d): a non-centre-cutting pass restart over a cleared core plunges, not refuses
body:
## What changed

`reenter` in `crates/motion/src/machining3d/reentry.rs` handles a pass restart in a 3D Pocket level. This PR changes its branch for a tool that is not centre-cutting:

- If the full disc is proved clear, the restart plunges. This is unchanged.
- If the core is not cleared (M11.3 core law, `plunge_law::into_solid`), the M11.3 fallback runs: helix, then the ramp along the pass, else the named refusal. This is unchanged.
- If the core is cleared but the outer disc is not proved clear, the fallback now runs on a copy of the path. The copy is kept if it has no refusal and is clean (no plunge into uncut stock, no crossing of a posted move). Otherwise the restart plunges, and a note names the plunge.

The centre-cutting branch is unchanged. The decision is in `docs/decisions/3885-non-cc-reentry.md`.

## Cause

#3857 applied the full-disc test to all tools. For a tool that is not centre-cutting, a restart over a cleared core then went to the M11.3 fallback. Where no helix or ramp fits, that fallback refuses the operation. Before #3857, the same restart was a legal plunge by the core law. So the change refused a legal program.

## Tests

The new pins are in `crates/motion/src/machining3d/reentry.rs` (`camcraft-motion` lib). Each test calls `reenter` with a hand-built level. The tool has a radius of 3 mm and is not centre-cutting.

- `machining3d::reentry::tests::a_non_centre_cutting_restart_over_a_cleared_core_plunges_without_room`: an earlier cut 1 mm from the axis clears the core. No helix or ramp fits. The test asserts no refusal, a plunge, and the note. It is red on unchanged upstream/main with this text: `entry refused: the tool is not centre-cutting - a pass start inside the level, and no helix or ramp fits onto Z -1.000`.
- `machining3d::reentry::tests::a_non_centre_cutting_restart_over_a_cleared_core_prefers_an_entry`: the same restart with room takes a helix or ramp, with no plunge into the material.
- `machining3d::reentry::tests::a_non_centre_cutting_restart_over_solid_core_is_refused_without_room`: the earlier cut is 2 mm from the axis, outside the 1.5 mm core reach. The refusal stays, with its name.

Mutation results:

- Upstream code: `..._plunges_without_room` fails. The fix makes it pass.
- Remove the `refused` guard: `..._plunges_without_room` fails.
- Skip the core-law check (`if false`): `..._over_solid_core_is_refused_without_room` fails.
- Always plunge over a cleared core (the old core-only law): `..._prefers_an_entry` fails.
- The fix is restored after each mutation, and all 5 `reentry` tests pass.

body:
Stacked on #3900 (U1). The base is `main`, because #3900 is a fork branch. The diff of U2 alone: https://github.com/qsmits/Camcraft/compare/be7168455...issue/3893-tool-library-editor

## What changed

U2 of #3663: you edit a tool in the tool library window.

- A tool opens in the window's editor. The list folds into a rail on the left ("All tools" and one row for each tool).
- The editor has two tabs:
  - **Tool**: the type, the geometry and the kind rows. The tab calls `tool_settings_grid::geometry` (with `kind_rows`). It does not copy them.
  - **Details**: the material group, the catalog facts of #898 and the tool number. The tab calls `tool_settings_grid::catalog` (with `tool_catalog_rows::catalog_rows`).
- **Apply** queues the same commands as the Apply of Properties: `State::apply_tool_numbers` (`ChangeTool`, or `ReshapeTool` when a drawn cutter rides the change) and `push_number_if_changed` (`SetToolNumber`, only when the number changed). A geometry and catalog edit is one undo step.
- **Edit tool shape** opens the existing shape window. That window edits through the draft of Properties. Thus, when Properties shows a different tool, Properties first moves to the tool of the window.
- The window keeps its **own draft** (`ToolLibraryView::editor`). Properties keeps `State::tool_ui`. `State::with_library_draft` swaps the draft of the window (and its sync key) into `tool_ui` only while the window draws and applies. Each draft has its own `(name, doc_version)` key, so typing in one draft never resets the other.
- The "Edit" button of the Document list opens the tool in the window. A new window opens on the tool that Properties shows. A pick in the window does not change the selection or the subject of Properties.
- If the open tool goes out of the document, the editor closes and the full list shows again.
- Decision: `docs/decisions/3893-tool-library-editor.md`.

No new command. No MCP tool is owed. Properties keeps all its groups. The holder, the cutting data and the drawing come to the window in U3 to U5.

title: fix(motion): warn on start-side stand-in entries and a Plunge into stock
body:
**Update at 6e381cc81 (review rework):** A selected Arc on an Outside ring pass with no air room is now refused by name (`OUTSIDE_AIR_REFUSAL`). The op posts no ramp stand-in. The pins are now `outside_pocket_arc_without_air_is_refused` and `outside_pocket_selected_entry_keeps_one_warning`. The PR comment 7136819007 has the details and the gate results. Where the text below says that Arc keeps a ramp stand-in on Outside, this update replaces it.

## What changed

A plain 2D Pocket with "Pass starts at: Outside" and no stock known has no air room (#3746). Before this change, two entries were notes only:

- With Arc, a later pass start in material took a ramp along the pass (`descent_dive::entry_restart`).
- With Plunge, the pass link plunged into uncut stock with no note.

`entry_status_lines` dropped the notes, and no warning was posted.

Now, on a start-side ladder (`Motion::cleared_links`, the #3316 link law):

- Each named stand-in entry (a ramp, a helix, an axial dive or a plunge) writes the marker `ENTRY_STAND_IN_NOTE`. The op posts one advisory `Warning::EntryStandIn { at, entries }` that counts the stand-ins.
- A pass link that plunges into a pass start in material writes `PLUNGE_INTO_STOCK_NOTE`. The op posts one advisory `Warning::PlungeIntoStock`. If the op already posts `EntryNotRecommended` for the selected Plunge, it does not post this second warning. Thus the plunge is named once.
- `entry_status_lines` shows each stand-in note as a `warning: Entry: ... - fix: ...` line. The two marker notes add no line, because the op warning is already in the status area.
- MCP names the new kinds `entry_stand_in` and `plunge_into_stock`.

Decision: `docs/decisions/3884-start-side-entry-warnings.md`. Arc with no air room keeps a safe, named stand-in with a Warning. It does not refuse, because a refusal would refuse every plain Outside pocket that uses the default Arc and has no stock.

The new code is in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/entry_warn.rs`. The changes to `generate.rs` and `types.rs` add only a few lines each. Both files were already over 400 lines.

## Pinning tests

- `camcraft-motion` `pass_start_engagement::outside_pocket_arc_ramp_is_a_warning` (pin 1): the band pocket with no stock and Arc has named stand-ins, and has exactly one `EntryStandIn` warning that counts them.
- `pass_start_engagement::outside_pocket_plunge_into_stock_is_one_warning` (pin 2): the same pocket with Plunge has more than one plunge, and has exactly one warning that names the plunge.
- `camcraft-ui` lib `approach_page::top_stock_tests::each_stand_in_entry_is_a_warning_line` (pin 3): the four stand-in note forms from the review are warning lines.

Red first: the pins use the new API (`entry_warnings`, `entry_stand_ins`, the marker notes), so they do not compile on `main`. Without the API, main has no warning and no status line for these notes. The review of #3872 proved this with a probe.

## Gates

- Targeted pins: green.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` (`CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=6`): 324 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (76.7 min); `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.
- Heavy steps (P1 under the safety floor): `cargo xtask gate heavy --only "app heavy: offset_pass_start"` ok (1146 s); `--only "app heavy: pocket_pass_start"` ok (10 s).

## Not exercised

- No app-level test that reads the op warnings for this pocket. The op adds the result of `entry_warnings` with one line in `generate.rs`.
- The stand-ins of Auto ladders show as warning lines on the op page, but they post no op warning (out of scope; see the decision).

Changelog: A 2D Pocket with "Pass starts at" Inside or Outside now posts a warning for each entry that is not the selected one, and for a selected Plunge that plunges into uncut stock. Before, these were notes only.

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #3884

title: fix(post): refuse waterjet posting until the jet records exist
body:
## What changed

This PR takes option 1 of the issue. It refuses waterjet posting by name until the jet records (#1882) and the waterjet laws (#1885) exist.

- The post gate (`verification_report_by`) refuses each unsuppressed waterjet operation. The new clause is in `crates/app/src/posting_waterjet.rs`. The refusal names the missing items: the standoff height, the jet on/off records, the pierce dwell records and the waterjet laws.
- A user post that declares `serves = ["waterjet"]` goes through the same gate. It writes no NC file.
- The stock simulation skips waterjet operations, as it skips wire cuts (`crates/app/src/stock_sim_waterjet.rs`). The nozzle does not go into the dexel model or the stock playback.
- The program sim refuses its verdict by name: "waterjet stock removal is not judged". The post gate shows this on its visible not-judged line.
- The path notes say that the jet and dwell records are not implemented. They also give a note for a pierce on the kerf ring when the lead-in is zero.
- The waterjet page:
  - shows the zero lead-in consequence;
  - shows the compensation choice as "In control" (no G-code words);
  - gives each tab row its own name ("Tab 1 position").
- Decision file: `docs/decisions/3637-waterjet-safety.md`. It also records that the operation does not model corner slow-down, taper or kerf lag.

## Cause

The waterjet operation has no standoff height. Its CL has no jet on/off record and no dwell record. No law refused it. A user post that served waterjet got a path with the nozzle tip at the sheet top. The stock sim used the nozzle as a milling cutter, and no note said that it does not judge waterjet.

The first attempt failed `post_not_judged::not_judged_with_no_generator_verdict_blocks` two times. Its waterjet clause sent back the generic `program_ops` error. title: fix(mcp): require mutual token proof and line limits on UI link
body:
## What changed

The UI link on Windows and all platforms now verifies that the listening server owns the token before sending any tool calls:
1. `crates/app/src/mcp/link.rs`:
   - Added `token_proof(token, nonce, role)` using clean-room SipHash-2-4 to prove token ownership without transmitting raw tokens over the socket.
   - Updated `hello_line` and `hello_matches` for mutual challenge-response verification.
   - Added `pid_alive(pid)` using `OpenProcess` on Windows and `libc::kill(pid, 0)` on Unix.
2. `crates/app/src/mcp/link_client.rs`:
   - `open` generates a fresh nonce, validates the server's proof, and refuses unverified peers.
   - `call` bounds answer line reads to 16 MiB (`MAX_LINE`).
3. `crates/app/tests/mcp_live/ui_link.rs`:
   - Added `false_server_on_stale_entry_is_refused_with_no_tool_calls_sent`.

Recorded in `docs/decisions/3874-windows-stale-link.md`.

title: fix(motion): stop inter-level rapid at feed height above prior floor in 3D Pocket
body:
## What changed

This change ensures that rapids between levels in 3D Pocket stop at feed height above the last cut floor instead of reaching the floor with zero margin (#3671):
- Updated `camcraft_motion::machining3d::descent::from`: on levels with a previous cut, the descent starting plane adds `ap.plunge_height` (the operation's feed height) to `mat_top(lvl, a)`, capped under the traverse plane `lvl.tz`.
- The rapid between levels stops at this feed height above the prior floor; the remaining descent into the next level is fed (e.g. helical feed or linear ramp).
- Regenerated the example catalog case `3d/rough-finish` (`rough-finish.camproj` and `rough-finish.nc`). The lowest rapid in `3D Pocket1` now stops at Z12 (2 mm above the Z10 floor) instead of Z10.
- Added pinning test `interlevel_rapid_stops_at_feed_height_above_prior_floor` in `crates/app/tests/example_catalog/case_3d_rough_finish.rs`.
- Updated `examples/catalog/3d/rough-finish/README.md`.
- Added decision record `docs/decisions/3671-3d-pocket-interlevel-rapid-margin.md`.

## Readings

title: fix(2d): peck a contour dive deeper than one stepdown below the cut floor
body:
## What changed

A contour dive below its ring's first level pecks when it would cut more than one stepdown below the cleared floor. This applies to dives past tabs and wall-side graze dives, including tabbed bore entries.

Each peck feeds one stepdown, retracts above the material, and returns above the last depth before the next feed. One note describes the pecked entry. The uncut floor is the material top, or one stepdown above a lower ring's first level. The first level never pecks.

The floor check now proves coverage of the entire tool disc. An exact matching endpoint or plunge column proves coverage. An axis-aligned straight feed also proves coverage when the target centre lies on its centreline. Uncertain coverage counts as uncut material. The proof does not use finite samples or approximate arc chords.

The old 4,096-peck cap no longer permits a long final cut. Every required stepdown is retained within the existing contour depth limit.

The XY path, tab layout, leads, and level order stay the same.

## Cause

The levels above cut the lead-in start of a tab window only at the ring start. Other windows can start above a 2.5 mm crescent of uncut material. The original dive cut 18 mm below that floor. The stay-down ramp preset cut 13.5 mm at window 0.

The review also found an uncovered rim with a 0.002 mm perpendicular lead. The shortened sample radius missed it. The peck cap could append a 9.04 mm final cut for a 0.01 mm stepdown.

## Pins and mutation proof

The L-shape fixture is in `crates/motion/tests/contour_tab_entry.rs`. Its independent oracle now samples the actual tool radius and counts straight plunge columns. It measures circular sweeps analytically. Inscribed chords create artificial gaps at the full rim, so they no longer stand in for earlier flat arcs. The safety assertions stay the same.

- `no_contour_descent_goes_more_than_one_stepdown_below_the_disc_floor` checks all descents of four entry presets.
- `a_short_perpendicular_lead_pecks_below_the_uncut_rim` checks the public generator with a 0.002 mm lead and a 0.0001 mm tolerance.
- `an_offset_column_leaves_an_uncut_rim` checks a prior column that misses the actual rim.
- `an_offset_straight_cut_does_not_prove_full_disc_coverage` checks an offset straight sweep and a proven centreline case.
- `a_dive_beyond_4096_pecks_preserves_every_stepdown` checks all 5,000 depths down to Z-50 at a 0.01 mm stepdown.
- `first_router_part_posts_the_shipped_program` checks the shipped router NC file through the CLI. Before regeneration, `first_part_programs` had one pass and one failure: the router NC pin was red.

The window readings use `(depth below floor, crescent)`. Plunge windows 1 to 3 change from `(18.0, 2.5)` to `(4.5, 2.5)`. The stay-down window 0 changes from `(13.5, 2.5)` to `(4.5, 2.5)`. Lead None remains `(2.7, 0.0)`.

Mutation proof:

- Restoring the old sampler makes `an_offset_column_leaves_an_uncut_rim` and `an_offset_straight_cut_does_not_prove_full_disc_coverage` fail. The public pin `a_short_perpendicular_lead_pecks_below_the_uncut_rim` also fails: at `(10.152613, -3.002)`, the floor is Z0 and the dive reaches Z-18. Restoring the fix passes all five peck unit tests and all five public contour tests.
- Restoring the old cap makes `a_dive_beyond_4096_pecks_preserves_every_stepdown` fail: it returns 4,097 depths instead of 5,000. Restoring the fix passes that pin.
- Restoring the literal router NC file from reviewed head `3d1564e10` makes `first_router_part_posts_the_shipped_program` fail. Restoring the final NC file passes that exact pin. The restored file matches its saved byte hash. Both `first_part_programs` tests also pass.

This check required no hand resolution. The gates do not include those newer upstream commits.

The two failures identified stale expectations below. The program changes add pecked tab-window dives. Each program was regenerated with the repository tool. The full quick gate found two stale expectations:
