title: fix(sim): refuse a feed plunge deeper than one stepdown below the uncut floor
body:
## What changed

The verifier names a feed plunge that takes more than one stepdown of uncut material in one move (#3679, law (d3)).

- New law `camcraft_sim::verify::plunge_depth`: every non-rapid axial descent is judged against the floor that the cuts before it left under the full tool disc. The take is the move's own bite - the lesser of the move's start and that floor - so a tip that a rapid already stood inside stock answers for its own descent only. A dive from air keeps the full column reading.
- The gate is `VerifyContext::plunge_stepdown`, the `None` discipline: only the level-cutting kinds state a stepdown (2D Contour, Pocket, Offset2D, Slot, TrochoidalSlot, Adaptive2D, Pocket3D, MultiAxisRough, the staged Face). A tilted 3+2 frame keeps `None`.
- The finding is advisory by the #3525 pattern: `Warning::PlungeTooDeep { at, mm, limit_mm }`, MCP kind `plunge_too_deep`, UI line 227. The post is not held. The issue's crescent case (an 18 mm plunge beside stock that no level above cut) is named.
- The program ahead acquits a conviction: `acquit_plunge_by_prior` re-reads each finding against the prior program's surface, the same third term of the min that `acquit_by_prior` gives a rapid. The wiring in `generate.rs` cuts the prior grid when either law convicted.
- The slack stays the established `z_tol` alone. No wider slack was added: the 0.5 mm overage of the first commit was a floor error and a bite error, not a tolerance error.

## The six reconciled suites

The first commit (cc1bed29d) over-convicted six pre-existing app tests. All six keep their expected verdicts. No test was changed.

1. `vertical_rapid_stock.rs::a_vertical_rapid_into_a_taller_block_is_named_and_blocks_the_post` - the entry rapid broke the raw top and the feed below it took 2 mm. The bite reading acquits the feed; the rapid conviction stands and holds the post.
2. `vertical_rapid_stock.rs::a_dive_into_stock_an_earlier_face_removed_posts` - the face left Z 5 standing. The bite reading and the prior acquittal clear the dive.
3. `carried_stock_entry.rs` (both `assert_safe_entry` failures) - 18 trochoidal microlift plunges of 0.3 mm read the raw 10.5 column; the bite reading acquits them. The one contour plunge read 10.5 where the face had left 10.0, its stepdown exactly; the prior acquittal clears it.
4. `clearance_in_stock.rs::the_same_plane_over_stock_an_earlier_face_cut_down_holds_only_for_the_first_traverse` - the prior acquittal removes the advisory; the first traverse stands as before.
5. `top_stock.rs::facing_to_top_removes_the_height_warning_but_a_shallow_face_does_not` - the same face-acquitted dive; the warnings are empty again.
6. The slack question - the 0.5 mm overage was cured by the honest floor and the honest bite, not by a wider tolerance. The law keeps the established `z_tol`.

## Pinning tests

- `camcraft-sim` `plunge_depth` binary: the crescent dive is named (mm 18.0 against the 4.5 stepdown); a dive exactly one stepdown deep, a ring-entry dive in the kerf of the level above, a pecked dive and the `None` gate stay clean; the bite is pinned by `a_feed_that_a_rapid_already_stood_inside_stock_answers_for_its_own_bite_only` and `a_feed_plunge_buried_deeper_than_one_stepdown_is_named_for_its_own_bite`.

- `camcraft-app` `plunge_depth_tab`: the catalog case `2d/contour-tabs` names its three tab-window dives (6.0 mm against a 2.0 stepdown), advisory.
- The six reconciled suites above.

## What was not exercised

title: perf(sim): grow the column stock's cut history in place

### What changed

- `stock_sim::cut::simulate` no longer copies the column stock's whole cut history at the start of each call. It takes the history out, grows it with `Arc::make_mut`, and puts it back. `Arc::make_mut` copies the history only when another stock shares it.
- On a refusal, the code truncates the cuts to their old count and puts the history back. `add_ops` only appends cuts, so the stock stays as it was.
- The behaviour of a single call does not change. A program that is cut one move for each call is now linear in its moves, not quadratic.

### Readings

- New pin `a_call_grows_the_history_in_place` on the v0.26.0 code: FAILED (`simulate copied the history instead of growing it in place`). With this change: ok.
- 4000 one-move calls on a 200 x 200 column block (debug build, this machine): 1.649 s before, 0.514 s after. The stock is the same to the bit as the one-call cut, before and after.
- A 3-axis job of 137,940 moves on a 2541 x 2100 column stock, cut one move for each call: more than 1800 s before (stopped), 6 s after. The removed volume is the same to the bit as the one-call cut.

title: feat(multiaxis): stated rotary axis from the machine line, with a disagreed-face refusal
body:
﻿feat(multiaxis): stated rotary axis from the machine line, with a disagreed-face refusal

## What changed

Issue #2772, parts 1 and 2 of the plan in
`docs/decisions/2772-rotary-4axis-refusal.md`. The rotary kinds
(Rotary Contour, Rotary Parallel, Rotary Offset) read their rotation
axis from a STATEMENT first; today's free fit is the fallback, and
nothing stated keeps every behaviour bit for bit.

1. The stated-axis resolver, `camcraft_app::rotary_stated` over
   `camcraft_motion::multiaxis::axis_stated`:
   - the op's own `stated_axis` direction first, else the mounted
     machine's stated rotary lines (a stated `axis` vector, else the
     RS-274 letter's line - the index-swing clause's own
     `rotary_line` reading, so one law reads both doors);
   - each line anchored through the setup's work offset origin (the
     indexed post's setup law: the WCS sits on the rotary
     centreline), canonicalized the fit's own way (signed, pinned to
     the `o . u = 0` foot), so a part truly on the line keeps the
     fitted path move for move;
   - JUDGED, never trusted: the fit's own concurrency share,
     coarseness skip and bearing law about the stated line
     (`axis_stated::judged_any`). A disagreement refuses by name:
     the part's own fitted axis and the two acts that fix it when
     the model is a revolve placed off the line; the freeform's
     4-axis wording (with the pinned "share no rotation axis"
     words) when no axis fits at all. Never a silent fall back to a
     free fit when a line was stated. A stated line that leans or is
     no direction refuses by name, as the swing clause does.
2. The caller switch, stated first / fit fallback:
   - `fixture::rotary_axis_of` - feeds the sim's chord pass
     (`stock_sim_rotary::rotary_plan`), the first traverse and the
     post gate's struck-steel law (`fixture_struck`): all three
     follow with no change of their own;
   - `first_traverse::turned_axis` - already prefers the job axis,
     which is now the stated-or-fitted line;
   - `rotary_law::rotary_into` - the radial field verdict takes the
     job's resolved axis (`rotary_axis`), keeping its fail-closed
     Gouge for the nothing-known case;
   - `rotary_picks::usable` and the centre-cutting audit's
     `revolved_bar_stated` - judge and read the resolved axis;
   - the letter door `rotary_gate::letter_gate` (moved from
     generate.rs) - a stated line answers the letter without a fit,
     held to the machine inventory;
   - the three motion kernels grow `*_stated` entries
     (`rotary_contour_stated`, `rotary_parallel_over_stated`,
     `rotary_offset_stated`) that take the judged axis; the plain
     entries keep the fit inside, so turning, drilling and every
     existing golden path are untouched.
3. The op param: `stated_axis` on the three arms - a direction
   ratio, never unit-scaled (the machine file's own law for its
   `axis` vector), through the WCS origin, overriding the machine
   line. UI edit (the rotary page's Passes tab, an armed group of
   three direction numbers riding the existing EditOperationParams
   commit), MCP patch (`edit_operation`'s merge patch over the DTO,
   automatic), project round-trip (`stated_axis`, PROJECT_VERSION
   steps v77 -> v78: an older reader must refuse rather than drop
   the statement and turn the part about an axis the user never
   named).
4. The cache stamp: the op's own direction, the machine's stated
   lines and the WCS anchor enter the digest ONLY when a line is
   stated - no cached path of a document without one goes stale.

## The readings

- The WCS origin is the stated line's anchor: the post subtracts the
  work offset from world coordinates, so in program coordinates the
  rotary centreline passes through the WCS origin - the same law the
  index-swing clause and the lathe spindle law read.
- The judge is the fit's own (`axis.rs`'s `data_of` + `judge`): the
  tolerance, the 90% concurrency share, the coarseness skip and the
  bearing law, evaluated about the stated line instead of a candidate
  from the eigen search. On the reporter's helical rotor the judge
  fails and the radial raster stays LOCKED (the decision doc's law:
  its radial pose can gouge on helical lobes) - the disagreement
  refusal says so and names the 4-axis case.
- A machine whose work-turning rotary states no `axis` vector keeps
  today's fit (absent is not stated, never zero). A trunnion's
  work-turning pair is read in chain order and the first line the
  model holds wins, so a standing revolve takes the C and a lying
  one takes the A.

## Pinning tests

- motion `axis_stated_tests`: a revolve holds its stated line and
  reads the fitted axis bit for bit; the canonical line is signed
  and pinned; a stated line away from the part names the part's own
  axis; the helical screw refuses with the 4-axis wording; an empty
  mesh refuses like the fit.
- app `rotary_stated_axis`:
  `a_stated_machine_line_generates_the_fitted_path` (microARC 4 +
  laid revolve: move-for-move the fitted program),
  `the_millturns_stated_c_carries_the_standing_bar` (C answered
  without a fit, the stamp runs),
  `the_screw_rotor_on_a_stated_A_is_refused_by_name` (the radial
  kinds stay locked on the screw),
  `the_screw_rotor_without_a_stated_line_keeps_the_old_refusal`
  (the pinned "share no rotation axis" words untouched),
  `a_stated_line_away_from_the_part_names_the_parts_own_axis` (both
  the disagreement and the letter-door wordings),
  `a_stated_line_the_part_holds_on_a_machine_that_has_it_generates`
  (the op's own statement, either sign),
  `a_work_offset_move_moves_the_stated_line_and_refuses` (the
  anchor is the WCS's own position),
  `the_stated_axis_round_trips_the_project_file` (v78 round-trip,
  v77 steps up unstated),
  `a_v77_file_opens_and_a_newer_file_is_refused` (the version pin).
- app `rotary_gate`: `a_stated_line_answers_the_letter_without_a_fit`
  (the screw's fit refuses, the stated line still answers).
- app `rotary_field_parity`:
  `the_stated_axis_parallel_reads_the_radial_law` - the heavy-lane
  parity of the stated-A program (the field eye vs the radial law,
  `#[ignore]`d like its three siblings; the quick suite pins the
  path equality, this lane proves the stated axis flows the whole
  sim pipeline at the verdict class).
- The continuous 4-axis example regenerated at v78 (its op follows
  the microARC's stated line - the same path the fit reads).

## What was NOT exercised

- The heavy parity lane runs at a cut, not here (the quick gate
  pins the path equality instead).
- No UI pixel snapshot is touched (release-lane only).

## Not included (the issue stays open)

- The RADIAL DROP FINISH KERNEL and the radial-step roughing
  (decision part 3/4): the live claim on
  `mkinney:issue/2772-radial-drop` holds that work. This PR's
  disagreement refusal keeps the radial kinds locked on helical
  parts until that kernel can consume the stated axis safely.
- No 360-degree radial drop finish for Rotary Parallel, no
  Doosan/Fanuc posting of one - same slice.

Changelog: Rotary Contour, Rotary Parallel and Rotary Offset read a
stated rotation axis first (the operation's own direction, else the
machine's stated rotary line through the work offset origin), judged
against the model's faces - a part on the stated line cuts the fitted
path unchanged, a part whose faces disagree refuses by name (the
4-axis case named), and nothing stated keeps the fitted axis (v78
project files).

title: feat(gcode): add the camcraft-gcode reader crate for 3-axis RS-274 and ISO 6983 programs
body:
## What this PR does

This PR adds the new crate `crates/gcode` (`camcraft-gcode`). The crate reads RS-274/NGC and ISO 6983 3-axis milling programs. It gives `cl::Toolpath` sections and a 1-based line map. It refuses unsupported words by name and line number.

- The crate depends on `camcraft-cl`, `camcraft-geometry` and `thiserror` only.
- It decodes the modal groups, `I`/`J`/`K` and `R` arcs in `G17`/`G18`/`G19`, and the canned cycles `G73`, `G81`, `G82`, `G83`, `G84`, `G85`, `G86`, `G89` with `G98`/`G99` and `L`.
- It splits sections at `T`/`M6`. It reads `S`, `M3`-`M5`, `M0`-`M2`, `M30`, `G4`, `G61`, `G64`, `G53`, `G28` and `G30`.
- It refuses `G41`/`G42`, macros (`G65`, `M98`, `#`), probing (`G31`, `G38.2`), `R` full circles, a missing `G20`/`G21`, a missing reference position, and `A`/`B`/`C`.

Sources: RS-274/NGC (NISTIR 6556), ISO 6983, and the public controller documents that `crates/gcode/src/dialect.rs` names for the dwell and arc presets. No other parser code was used.

## Held work

- Commit `711314efd` by Mike Kinney, from `mkinney:issue/2217-camcraft-gcode`. It has the crate, its 9 tests, the decision file and the gate plan entries.
- This PR keeps that commit and its author unchanged. A merge commit (`db23cf9bd`) joins it to main `60376ccbb`.

## Added after the held commit

- `db23cf9bd` merge: the conflict resolution (next section).
- `75b33ace3` `test(xtask)`: two xtask tests of main list the crates by hand. `heavy_plan_tests::reach_follows_the_crate_dependencies` now expects `gcode` in the reach of `geometry`. `step_tests::batch_prebuild_leaves_suite_steps_fresh_with_truck_dev_dep` now writes a stub `crates/gcode`. `Cargo.lock` takes the version `0.25.0` for `camcraft-gcode`.
- `92627aef0` `test(gcode)`:
  - Each gcode suite has a `Gate map: covers camcraft_gcode::{..}` line. Quick then selects the suites for a change in each `crates/gcode/src` module.
  - The new suite `degenerate_input` checks malformed programs. Each one gives a value or a refusal, with no panic and no hang.
  - The decision file records the merge.

## Conflict resolution

All three conflicts were lists. No logic hunk had a conflict.

- Root `Cargo.toml`: the `members` line has main's `"crates/gpu"` and the held `"crates/gcode"` (after `"crates/cl"`). The `camcraft-gcode` workspace dependency merged without a conflict.
- `xtask/src/plan.rs`: `BATCH_CRATES`, `ALL_CRATES` and `CLIPPY` have `"gcode"` after `"cl"` and main's `"gpu"` after `"app"`.
- `xtask/src/tests.rs`: the release step count keeps main's known-fail `checks` term. It uses the held `plan::ALL_CRATES.len()` in place of the fixed `10`.
- `Cargo.lock` merged without a conflict.

## New crate edges

- `camcraft-gcode -> camcraft-cl`: `ArcPlane`, `Cycle`, `CycleKind`, `MoveKind`, `PathBuilder`, `Toolpath`, `lattice`.
- `camcraft-gcode -> camcraft-geometry`: `geo2d::Point2`, `Point3`, `units::{from_display, Unit, MM_PER_INCH}`.
- `docs/decisions/2217-camcraft-gcode.md` gives the imported items, the reason that a caller cannot pass the values in, and the rebuild impact. No crate depends on `camcraft-gcode` yet.

## Review fixes (review of `92627aef0`)

Commit `cb4acfadd` fixes the 11 review items. The merge `e0cc82c99` takes current `origin/main` (`44903e15e`); it merged with no conflict. The decision file has one entry for each item.

1. G73/G83: each peck must move deeper, at most 4096 pecks; one cycle block emits at most 100 000 moves.
2. Numeric domain: lengths and points are finite and inside +/-1e6 mm after conversion and arithmetic; caller options are checked. New errors `OutOfRange` and `InvalidOptions`.
3. One frame rule for G54-G59, G28, G30 and G53 (cursor moves into the new frame; unknown origins are refused).
4. Canned cycles run in G17 only; G18/G19 cycles and plane changes in a cycle are refused.
5. Spindle, coolant, length- and work-offset changes after a move start a new section.
6. Cycle state holds over repeated cycle codes and bare blocks.
7. G89 feeds out to the clear level.
8. G90.01 is refused; G90.10 is G90.1.
9. Haas `P10` is ms, `P10.` is s.
10. The gpu clippy failure is fixed on main by `4cc0638ee`; the merge brings it in. No gpu change in this PR.
11. One directory suite: `crates/gcode/tests/parse/`.

## Tests

All tests are in one directory suite, `crates/gcode/tests/parse/` (`main.rs` holds the Gate map and the shared 5 s time-limit helper). No new top-level test binary. The `#[test]` count went from 10 to 37.

- `three_axis` (was `gcode_3axis.rs`, 7 tests). `modal_groups_track_and_sections_split_on_tool_changes` now has G55/G56 origins and pins the start of tool 2 in the G56 frame.
- `dialects_and_planes` (2), `degenerate_input` (1): moved, unchanged.
- `cycle_bounds` (item 1): `peck_cycles_near_1e20_refuse_and_never_spin`, `peck_cycles_without_f64_progress_refuse_by_line`, `peck_count_over_4096_per_hole_refuses`, `expansion_over_pecks_and_repeats_is_bounded`.
- `numeric_domain` (item 2): `huge_finite_axis_words_refuse_by_line`, `incremental_sum_past_the_domain_refuses`, `huge_arc_radius_refuses_instead_of_a_straight_move`, `huge_feed_after_inch_conversion_refuses`, `values_inside_the_domain_still_parse`, `bad_caller_options_refuse_before_line_one`.
- `frames` (item 3): `g54_to_g55_keeps_the_machine_move`, `nonzero_origins_move_the_cursor_on_every_axis`, `offset_change_after_motion_without_origins_refuses`, `g28_and_g30_use_the_machine_origin_of_the_active_offset`, `g28_without_a_known_work_origin_refuses`.
- `cycle_rules` (items 4, 6, 7): `cycles_in_g18_and_g19_refuse_before_expansion`, `plane_change_while_a_cycle_is_active_refuses`, `repeated_cycle_code_keeps_sticky_r_and_z`, `g98_initial_level_survives_g99_and_repeated_codes`, `incremental_sticky_depths_repeat_from_the_same_levels`, `g89_feeds_to_the_clear_level_and_g85_feeds_to_r`.
- `sections` (item 5): `spindle_start_after_the_first_move_starts_a_section`, `every_state_change_between_moves_is_kept`, `a_repeated_equal_state_word_keeps_one_section`.
- `codes_and_dwell` (items 8, 9): `decimal_codes_keep_their_place_value`, `haas_g04_p_without_a_point_is_ms_and_with_a_point_is_s`, `haas_cycle_dwell_uses_the_same_rule`.

## Gate

### Final result on `16e1ff8c7` (the current head)

- Command: `CAMCRAFT_NO_SEED=1 cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`, run on the head `16e1ff8c7` itself. Started 2026-11-24 00:37 UTC. Toolchain `rustc 1.99.1` (stable). Budget: 10 jobs.

title: feat(wire): post a convex DXF loop of tangent lines and arcs as native wire EDM job files
body:
Stacked on #2992. Review the [changes above the #2992 head](https://github.com/qsmits/Camcraft/compare/db8a61aba...fa31e7120).

## What changed

A Wire Contour punch can now use one selected closed DXF chain that is a convex loop of tangent lines and arcs. Before, only a circle or a racetrack was possible (#2022). The native wire EDM job keeps each nominal line end and each arc centre.

The port puts the work of #2993 on the current frame:

- Geometry (`camcraft-geometry`): `wire_round_profile::WireProfile` holds a `RoundProfile` (circle or racetrack, #2022) or a new `TangentProfile`. `WireProfile::from_chain` reads a circle or a racetrack first, so `CIRCLE20` and `RACE20` do not change. Every other chain must pass the tangent proof: tangent joints, counter-clockwise arcs of at most 180 degrees, arc turns that total one revolution, radii from 0.5 to 20 mm, at most 128 segments. The preview polygon encloses each arc within 0.000025 mm and is checked against the analytic support of the loop (at most 2,048 vertices).
- App (`camcraft-app`): `SelectedWireChain::wire_profile` replaces `round_profile`. `agie_sketch_job` returns the `WireProfile` and checks the rest of the drawing against the exact bounds of the loop plus the 0.4 mm rough and wire margin.
- Post (`camcraft-post`): the new `agie/tangent_profile.rs` gives the same `ArcBlock` list and `PunchSetup20` as `round_profile.rs` (#2978). Each joint and centre must be on the five-decimal grid within 1e-9 mm. No value is rounded. The post checks the exact squared radius at both arc ends and the tangent direction at each joint in integer grid units. The entry is perpendicular to a straight side parallel to X or Y, from the waste side, with 3 mm of straight on each side of the seam. The stock must have 0.4 mm beyond the exact bounds of the loop. The quality is CCB030 through `contour::punch_setup`, with no own quality object (#2984). `export_round_with_review` now takes a `&WireProfile`.
- The old writer file of the PR (`tangent_profile.rs` on the deleted `Work`) and its new top-level test binary `agie_dxf.rs` are not used.

## Readings on the emulated control

We imported `ROUND20` and `THREEARC` on an offline copy of the Classic Cut 2S control. No physical cut was made.

- Both jobs: the ISO and SBL bytes on the control disk agree with the source. The work shows `CCB030[0]` after import. FORMALCHECK shows one error, `Technologie : te definiëren`. The quality page shows CCB030, Ra 0.30, Tkm 1.0, Te 1.5. The TECCUT header shows Dia 0.25, H 20, Ra 0.30, Tkm 1.0, Te 1.5, row 0199. After `Toewijzen` the work shows `CCB030[4]` with the offsets 245, 155, 140 and 134 µm. FORMALCHECK then gives `geen fouten`. The only warnings are `Uitgekozen opties : 131072` and `Referentiewaarden : te definiëren`.
- `ROUND20`: the J00 keeps the four arc centres (14, −8), (16, 10), (−14, 8) and (−16, −10) on every pass. The rough radii are 6.245 and 4.245 mm, then 6.155/4.155, 6.140/4.140 and 6.134/4.134 mm. The separation is from X0 to X−1: 1.000 mm.
- `THREEARC`: the J00 keeps the centres (24, 0), (0, 18) and (0, 0) on every pass. The oblique side moves along its normal by each offset. The separation is from X12 to X11: 1.000 mm.

## Pinning tests

- `camcraft-app` `agie_native` (module `tangent`): `a_mixed_radius_loop_posts_each_nominal_arc_and_the_checked_setup`, `an_oblique_tangent_side_joins_three_distinct_arcs` (goldens `ROUND20.ISO` and `THREEARC.ISO`; the SBL is the checked `CCSEP20` setup with only the stem and the hole changed), `a_short_inner_offgrid_edge_or_folded_loop_publishes_nothing`.
- `camcraft-post` lib (`agie::tangent_profile_tests`): the ISO of both loops, and the refusals for a short or inner entry, an off-grid joint, a thin stock margin, a die and a 40 mm plate.
- `camcraft-geometry` lib (`wire_round_profile::tests`, `wire_round_profile::tangent::tests`): the tangent proof, the bounds, the preview, and the refusals for a folded loop, a corner and a circle radius.
- `camcraft-app` `agie_native` (module `quality`): `ra035_refuses_a_group_an_arc_punch_a_die_and_a_cutoff` now also refuses the Ra 0.35 request on the tangent `rounded-punch` example. No control data covers CCB035 on an arc punch.
- The existing goldens `CIRCLE20`, `RACE20` and `CCSEP20` do not change.

Goldens added: `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/agie-native/ROUND20.ISO` and `THREEARC.ISO`. The other golden differences against main belong to the parent #2992. No golden that is on main changes.

Screenshots: no UI change.

`cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` on `fa31e7120`: 1,201 steps in 50 minutes, 0 failed, 0 stalled. Strict Clippy (`-D warnings`, all targets) passed for `camcraft-post`, `camcraft-geometry`, `camcraft-app` and `camcraft-ui`. No heavy lane ran (P6). The ISO bytes of `ROUND20` and `THREEARC` are the same as the bytes that the control read.

- A die opening with tangent arcs. The post refuses it.

title: feat(wire): group up to nine captured punches on one plate
body:
Stacked on #2981 (head `7a97b0f57`). #2972, #2974, #2978 and #2979 are merged on main. Review the [changes above the parent](https://github.com/qsmits/Camcraft/compare/7a97b0f5716779507972a6fff82cdb483e2b2f1f...issue/2980-agie-punch-groups).

This PR is ported onto the zero-step setup frame of #2984 and the stack up to #2981. The old writer of this PR is gone. The old head was `c81cfd1d4`.

## What changed

- A punch group holds 2 to 9 complete modeled punches on one 20 mm plate. The limit is `agie_setup::MAX_PUNCH_WORKS` (9). It applies in these three places:
  - `PunchGroup20::encode` (was `GROUP_WORKS = 2`);
  - `agie::export_group_with_review` (was `jobs.len() != 2`);
  - the app dispatch in `posting_agie.rs` (was `1..=2`).
- Each work has its own ISO (`<group>1.ISO` to `<group>9.ISO`), its own SBR line, its own work `CUTn` and its own threading hole. All works refer to the ONE `CCB030` quality object of the piece (#2984). The old PR body said "each work gets its own resident quality object". This port does not do that, because #2984 showed that different quality names can bind to different resident data.
- The clear-band check compares every pair of works, not only neighbours in the program. The message names the two works, for example `The works TRIO201 and TRIO203 share a cutting area`.
- A punch group refuses a placed drawing, as a die group does.
- Die groups stay at two openings. The PR has no control evidence for larger die groups. `encode_die`, the post and the app refuse a third opening with their own message.
- New messages: `SetupError::GroupWorks`, the post group refusal and the app count refusal state the new limits.
- New examples `examples/agie/punch-trio.camscript` and `punch-grid.camscript`. They use the post name `Native wire EDM job files`.
- The user guide section is now **Group captured punches**.

## Value sources

No new control value. The 20 mm offsets (245, 155, 140 and 134 µm), the TECCUT row and all SBL fields are those of the checked pair `PAIR20` (#2961). Only the work name, the resource and the hole change for each work. The stock (120 × 100 × 20 mm), the 32 mm pitch, the 14 × 16 mm punch (`pair-left.obj`) and the holes 13 mm left of each centre are from the examples of this PR.

## Readings

Emulated Classic Cut 2S, 2026-11-24, throwaway clone of the practice image (base SHA-256 unchanged, clone deleted). The files of this frame were imported, and the bytes on the guest disk were identical.

| | TRIO20 (3 works) | NINE20 (9 works) |
|---|---|---|
| After import | `CCB030[0]`, own `stp1` and ISO on each work | same, 9 distinct resources |
| Quality on each work | CCB030 Ra 0.30, Tkm 1.0, Te 1.5, options off | same, also on CUT9 |
| TECCUT | row 0199, `estbca25nnn060b030020`, T100 on each work (20 mm row) | same |
| After TECCUT | `CCB030[4]` on each work | same |
| FORMALCHECK | `geen fouten`; warnings `Uitgekozen opties : 131072`, `Referentiewaarden : te definiëren` | same |
| J00 cut blocks | 24 | 72 |
| Cut order | profile passes of CUT1..CUT3, then the 1.000 mm separations | profile passes of CUT1..CUT9, then the separations |
| Transits between works | head up (Z53 or Z80) only | same, 37 moves, none below Z53 |
| Cutting envelopes | 3 pairs, 0 overlap | 36 pairs, 0 overlap |

The quality problem of the old run (the first and the ninth generic quality names bound to different resident targets) does not occur: there is only one quality object.

## Pinning tests

- `camcraft-post` lib: `group_count_tests::every_group_size_has_its_own_file_work_and_hole_and_one_quality`, `a_tenth_punch_or_a_third_die_opening_writes_nothing`, `a_collision_of_works_that_are_not_neighbours_names_the_pair`; `group_tests::a_group_refuses_a_die_two_works_on_one_area_another_stock_or_no_separation` (updated).
- `camcraft-post` `agie_safe_setup` (module `group`): `trio_and_grid_files_match_their_goldens_with_one_quality` (new goldens `TRIO20.SBL/SBR`, `NINE20.SBL/SBR`), `a_group_refuses_its_unqualified_inputs` (ten works); module `die_group`: three distinct openings refused.
- `camcraft-app` `agie_native`: `group::three_model_owners_post_the_trio_goldens` (ISO goldens `TRIO201..203.ISO`), `group::nine_model_owners_post_the_grid_goldens_with_their_own_iso_and_hole`, `group::a_tenth_work_an_unowned_model_a_shared_source_or_a_far_collision_writes_nothing`, `die_group::a_missing_shared_or_unsafe_die_work_writes_nothing` (three die works).
- Unchanged bytes: the PAIR20, DUODI20, CCSEP20, DIE20, LOWER20, RACE20, CIRCLE20, FINE20 and inspection goldens are not edited, and their tests pass.

## Gate (head `db8a61aba`)

The head merges the #2981 head `7a97b0f57`, which merges `origin/main` `83e5e8a37` (with #2972, #2974, #2978, #2979 and the fix of #3774). The merges have no hand edits, except the one resolved conflict of the test move (`crates/post/tests/agie_safe_setup/group.rs`, merge `877007b02`).

- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-geometry -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-post --test agie_safe_setup`: 22 passed (on `052e01afa`).
- `git merge-tree --write-tree HEAD origin/main` (`582981bfa`): clean.
- No heavy lane, by AGENTS.md (`P6`).

## Not exercised

- A tenth work, mixed punch and die groups, and die groups of more than two openings: refused, no control run.

Changelog: The native wire EDM post accepts groups of up to nine captured punches on one 20 mm plate. It checks the cutting areas of every pair of works and names the two works that meet. All works use one quality object.

## Test layout

This PR adds no new top-level test binary. The post setup tests are modules of the existing suite `agie_safe_setup`. The test count did not change.

body:
The parent PRs #2972, #2974, #2978 and #2979 are merged on main. This PR now merges `origin/main`, so its diff against main is the die pair only.

This PR is ported onto the zero-step setup of #2984. The quality-binding correction of #2984 now applies to the die pair: the piece has one CCB030 quality object, and both works refer to it. The old writer (`jescript.rs`) is gone. The PR ports the behaviour, not the old writer.

## What changed

- **App.** Two Wire Contour operations with the die side make a die group. Each operation selects the upper rim of one through-opening of the same modeled plate. The plate must be the only model, with no placed drawing. The plate must have exactly two through-openings, one for each operation. Each selected rim must match the full-height opening of the plate. The app reads the selected rim (`operation/agie_die.rs`). The plate check and the opening match are in `camcraft_geometry::die_opening` (`check_die_plate`, `matching_opening`), as AGENTS.md "app holds the document" requires. A single die job keeps its check and its message (exactly one through-opening).
- **Post.** `export_group_with_review` accepts two die openings as well as two punches. Both works must have the same side. A punch and a die in one group are refused. Each opening gets the existing die checks of #2957 (20 mm plate, convex opening, hole inside the opening, inward lead, reach and stock margin). The clear band check now covers die openings: the cutting area of each work holds the opening, its hole and 3 mm lead, the rough corner and the wire radius. The same opening selected twice fails this check.
- **Setup.** `PunchGroup20::encode_die` writes the control-checked group records of #2961 with `ID_PUNCH,c_die` on each work. `PunchGroup20::encode` (PAIR20) keeps its bytes and its review text. The die review text tells the operator to confirm `c_die` on each work, to keep each pass inside its own opening, to check that no cutting move crosses the plate between the openings, and to support each slug.
- The example `examples/agie/die-pair.camscript` uses the current post name. The decision file is `docs/decisions/2977-wire-die-pair.md`. The user guide section "Group two die openings in one plate" has the control readings.

## Value sources

No setup value is new. Each value comes from a control-checked setup:

- The group records, the work order `CUT1`, `CUT2` and the SBR layout: PAIR20 (#2961).
- The die side `c_die` and the 20 mm rule for a die: DIE20 (#2957).
- The one CCB030 quality object: #2984.
- The 1 mm separation, steel 0001, Berco Cut 0.25 and the 20 mm offsets 245, 155, 140 and 134 µm: the existing QN2 table (#2954).
- The plate, the two rims and the threading holes X-35.5 Y0 and X24.5 Y0: the example of this PR.

## Readings

The ported DUODI20 job was imported on the emulated Classic Cut 2S control (a throwaway clone of the practice image; the base image SHA-256 did not change). No physical cut was made.

- The two ISO files and the SBL arrived on the control byte for byte.
- After import: `CUT1` and `CUT2` show `CCB030[0]`. The formal check gave one error for each work: `Technologie : te definiëren`.

- The formal check of the piece: `Controleresultaat: geen fouten`. The warnings are the same as for PAIR20: `Uitgekozen opties : 131072` on each work and `Referentiewaarden : te definiëren`.
- GRAFICHECK (J00): ten cut blocks in this order: the main pass of `CUT1`, the main pass of `CUT2`, the separation of `CUT1`, the separation of `CUT2` (Y0 to Y1, 1.000 mm), the three trims of `CUT1`, the three trims of `CUT2`. The machine moves between the works only in transit blocks with the head up. All cutting points stay in their own opening: `CUT1` X-42.366 to X-17.634, `CUT2` X17.634 to X42.366. No cutting point is in the plate between the openings (X-17.5 to X17.5).

## What changed

This PR is ported onto the zero-step setup of #2984. The job names the requested work quality. It arms no technology. The operator assigns TECCUT on the control after the review, as for every other job.

- The new Wire Contour condition `AGIE_BERCO_RA035` requests quality `CCB035`: Ra 0.35, Te 1.50 and Tkm 1.00 µm, with the speed option set and the other two options disabled: `JE_CreateQuality(je_piece,"CCB035","0.35,1.50,1.00,T,F,F",je_q1)`. With the speed option, the control preselects the Ra 0.35 technology `estbca25nsn060b035020` (TECCUT header `TYPE:VS`). The job still arms no technology. The condition `AGIE_QN2` requests `CCB030`, as before.
- `camcraft_post::agie_setup::Quality` (`Ccb030`, `Ccb035`) is on the private `Piece`. The piece creates one quality object with that name. `PunchSetup20::encode_quality` is the only way to request `CCB035`. `encode`, `encode_die`, `PunchGroup20` and `CutoffSetup20` keep `CCB030`.
- `CCB035_OFFSETS_UM` has one row: 20 mm, five passes, 234, 189, 154, 139 and 129 µm (main cut and four trims). `Quality::offsets_um` returns all passes, and `Quality::rough_um` gives the main cut. The contour checks (clearance, miter and entry) use the main-cut offset of the selected quality: 234 µm for `CCB035`. The 0.4 mm stock margin does not change (0.234 + 0.125 rounds up to 0.4). `CCB030` keeps its 4-pass table and its bytes.

The user guide says the same. It names the technology, not a TECCUT number: the first TECCUT column is a match distance, not a row id.
- `camcraft_post::agie::export_punch_with_review` takes the quality. With `Ccb030` it is `export_with_review`.

- Ra 0.35, Te 1.50 and Tkm 1.00: the Fine+ values of the MIT Agie Processor quality presets, as in the original PR.

body:
Stacked on #2972. Review the [changes above the parent](https://github.com/qsmits/Camcraft/compare/f99a9d736...issue/2961-agie-multiple-works).

Process change: yes

## What changed

This PR posts two independently captured punches on one 20 mm plate as one native wire EDM job. It is ported onto the zero-step setup writer of #2984 and onto the #2955, #2964, #2968, #2969 and #2972 ports. The old branch wrote its own SBL through `jescript.rs`. That writer is deleted on main, and this port does not use it.

- **Piece writer (post).** `agie_setup/piece.rs` now takes one `Piece` (stem, stock, height) and a list of `Work` (ISO stem, side, start point, exit point). It writes one quality `CCB030`, one group and the works `CUT1..n` in a loop. Each work refers to the same quality object (`ID_QUALITY,je_q1`) and has its own `ID_GEOMETRY`, `stp1` and `ASDELETE` call. The single-work SBL is byte-identical to before.
- **Group setup (post).** The new `agie_setup::PunchGroup20` takes the group stem, the stock, the 20 mm height and two `GroupPunch` entries (ISO stem and start hole). It refuses another number of works, a repeated or invalid ISO stem, a height other than 20 mm, stock outside the 350 × 250 mm span and a hole that is not completely inside the stock.
